name: Salesforce Administrator (CRT-101)
description: Core admin exam: configuration, security, automation, data management, reporting, and Service/Sales Cloud.

questions.text: Users at Cloud Kicks are reporting different options when uploading a custom picklist on the Opportunity object based on the kind of opportunity. Where should an administrator update the option in the picklist?
questions.explanation:
Record types let you offer different business processes, picklist values, and page layouts to different users on the same object. When a single object (like Opportunity) needs to behave differently for different "kinds" of records, record types are the standard way to model that.

Picklist value sets only define the master list of available values; they don't decide which subset to show on a record. Record types let you map each type to a filtered subset of values for any picklist. Lookup filters and Fields & Relationships are unrelated — they manage relationship constraints and field metadata, not picklist visibility.

questions.text: An administrator has been asked to update a flow that was created as part of a recent update. When the administrator opens the flow for editing, the Flow toolbox offers only four elements: Assignment, Decision, Get Records, and Loop. What would cause this?
questions.explanation:
Before-save record-triggered flows run inside the same database transaction as the save itself, so they can update fields on the saving record without a second DML. Because of this constrained execution context, they intentionally support only a limited toolbox: Assignment, Decision, Get Records, and Loop.

If a flow opens with only those four elements, you are looking at a Before Save flow. The other clues — screen flow, inactive version, activated version — don't restrict the toolbox the way the trigger configuration does. To get the full set of elements (subflows, Create/Update/Delete, screens, etc.), use a different trigger type such as After Save or autolaunched.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The flow is a screen flow.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The version of the flow is inactive.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The flow is a before save flow.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The version of the flow is activated.

questions.text: An administrator wants to create a form in Salesforce for users to fill out when they lose a client. Which automation tool supports creating a wizard to accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation:
Flow Builder is Salesforce's primary low-code automation tool and the only one designed to walk a user through a multi-step form. Screen Flows let you collect input, branch on decisions, look up data, and write records — all in a guided wizard that lives inside Lightning, mobile, or Experience Cloud sites.

Process Builder runs in the background and has no UI. Approval Process drives review and routing, not data entry. Outbound Message just calls a SOAP endpoint. None of those build a wizard. Flow is the right pick for any "collect info from a user across screens" requirement.

questions.text: The Client services and customer support teams share the same profile but have different permission sets. The Custom Object Retention related list needs to be restricted to the client services team on the Lightning record page layout. What should the administrator use to fulfil this request?
questions.explanation:
Component Visibility on Lightning App Builder lets you hide or show any component on a record page based on filters — fields on the record, the running user's profile, permission sets, or device form factor. It's a no-code way to tailor what each user sees without creating extra page layouts.

In this scenario the two teams share a profile but differ by permission set. Page Layout Assignment can only branch on profile + record type, so it can't separate them. Sharing settings control record access, not component visibility, and Record Type Assignment doesn't apply when both teams use the same profile/record type. Component Visibility filtered by permission set is the precise lever.

questions.text: The VP of sales at Universal Containers wants to prevent members of the sales team from changing an opportunity to a date in the past. What should an administrator configure to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Validation rules evaluate a formula at save time and block the save (with an error message) when the formula returns true. They are the standard way to enforce data quality and business policy on field values.

Here the rule's formula compares Close Date to TODAY() and fires if the new value is in the past. Assignment Rules route records to owners; Field-Level Security controls visibility, not validity; Approval Processes are for review workflows. Only validation rules can prevent the save outright based on a field comparison.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to track ROI for contacts that are key stakeholders for opportunities. The VP of Sales requested that this information be accessible on the opportunity and available for reporting. Which two options should the administrator configure to meet these requirements? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Opportunity Contact Roles capture the contacts associated with a deal and the part each played (Decision Maker, Economic Buyer, Influencer, etc.). Once roles are populated they roll into reports so you can attribute revenue and ROI to the people involved.

To make this work end-to-end you typically customize the Contact Role picklist values to match your business and add the Opportunity Contact Roles related list to the Opportunity page layout so reps actually see and edit it. Campaign Member roles relate to marketing membership, not opportunity influence — they don't satisfy the "stakeholders for opportunities" requirement.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add the Campaign Member related list to the Opportunity page layout.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Add the Opportunity Contact Role related list to the Opportunity page layout.

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks has a Custom picklist field on Lead, which is missing on the Contact when leads are converted. Which two items should the administrator do to make sure these values are populated? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
During lead conversion, Salesforce copies the lead's fields onto the new Account, Contact, and Opportunity records — but only for fields you have explicitly mapped. For custom fields, this means two steps: create a corresponding custom field on the target object (Contact in this case), then map the lead field to it under Setup > Object Manager > Lead > Fields & Relationships > Map Lead Fields.

Validation rules and required-field flags don't transfer values during conversion. The fix is structural: add the destination field, then tell Salesforce which lead field flows into it.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a custom picklist field on Contact.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Update the picklist value with a validation rule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Map the picklist field on the Lead to the Contact.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set the picklist field to be required on the Lead Object.

questions.text: Universal Containers is trying to improve the user experience when searching for the right status on a case. The company currently has one support process that is used for all record types on cases. The support process has 10 status values. Service reps say they never need more than five depending on what kind of case they are working on. How should the administrator improve on the current implementation?
questions.explanation:
A Support Process is a subset of Case Status values bound to a record type. By creating multiple support processes — one per case kind — you give each record type its own short, relevant status list, instead of forcing reps to scroll past values that don't apply to their case.

Reducing the global picklist to five would punish other teams who do need those values. Edits to the record type don't change which statuses are offered (that's the support process's job), and a screen flow in the utility bar is overkill when the picklist itself can be tailored per record type.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reduce the number of case status values to five.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a Screen Flow that shows only the correct values for status and surface the flow in the utility bar of the console.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Review which status choices are needed for each record type and create support processes for each that is necessary.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Edit the status choices directly on the record type.

questions.text: When a Sales rep clicks a button on an opportunity, a simple discount calculator screen should be launched. Which automation tool should an administrator use to build this discount calculator screen?
questions.explanation:
Flow Builder Screen Flows are the right tool whenever you want a user to click a button and step through a calculation or form. They can take inputs, run formulas, and present results — exactly what a discount calculator needs.

Workflow Rules and Process Builder are background-only and have no UI. Platform Events are pub/sub messaging plumbing, not a calculator. A button-launched Screen Flow placed on the Opportunity page or as a quick action is the canonical pattern.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to initiate expense reports from Salesforce to the external HR system. This process needs to be reviewed by managers and directors. Which two tools should an administrator configure? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Quick Actions are the gateway by which a user kicks off a process — they expose the form or button in the record's actions section. Approval Processes layer on top with multi-step routing, so managers and directors can review the request before it advances.

Outbound Messages are point-to-point integrations and don't model approvals. Email Alerts only notify; they don't gate a record on review. Pairing Quick Action (entry point) with Approval Process (review) is the standard build for "submit and route".

questions.text: Cloud Kicks is working on a better way to track its product shipments utilizing Salesforce. Which field type should an administrator use to capture coordinates?
questions.explanation:
Geolocation is a compound field type designed to hold latitude/longitude coordinates. With it, distance functions like DISTANCE() become available in formulas and reports, and you can drive map components and proximity queries off the field.

Geofence and Custom Address are not standard Salesforce field types in this context, and External Lookup is for cross-org references via Salesforce Connect, not for storing coordinates. Geolocation is the right primitive when you literally need lat/long on a record.

questions.text: What are two considerations an administrator should keep in mind when working with Salesforce objects? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Salesforce ships with standard objects (Account, Contact, Opportunity, Lead, Case, etc.) that cover the most common CRM scenarios. Beyond that you can model anything else with custom objects you create yourself — and Salesforce treats those custom objects as first-class citizens.

You cannot create a new "standard" object — the standard set is fixed by Salesforce — but custom objects are unlimited (within edition limits) and support master-detail just like standard ones do. So the two correct considerations are that standard objects come pre-built and that you can extend the model with new (custom) objects.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Custom and standard objects have standard fields.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Standard objects are included with Salesforce.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A new standard object can be created.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Only standard objects support master-detail relationships.

questions.text: Users have noticed that when they click on a report in a dashboard to view the report details, the values in the report are different from the values displayed on the dashboard. What are the two reasons this is likely to occur? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Dashboards display cached data from the last refresh, while clicking through to a source report runs the report live with the viewer's permissions. Two things can therefore make the numbers diverge: the dashboard hasn't been refreshed since data changed, or the running user (whose security context drives the dashboard) sees a different slice of records than the viewer.

Switching the running user or scheduling a refresh resolves both. The report itself is always live when opened, so "report needs to be refreshed" is a non-issue — and folder access would block the click entirely, not produce different numbers.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The report needs to be refreshed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The dashboard needs to be refreshed.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The current user does not have access to the report folder.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The running dashboard user and viewer have different permissions.

questions.text: The marketing team wants a new picklist value added to the Campaign Member Status field for the upsell promotional campaign. Which two solutions should the administrator use to modify the picklist field values? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Campaign Status and Campaign Member Status are two different picklists on two different objects. Campaign Status (Planned/In Progress/Completed/Aborted) is on Campaign and is edited like any other picklist in Object Manager. Campaign Member Status (Sent, Responded, Registered, Attended…) is per-campaign and is edited via the Campaign Member Statuses related list on the campaign page.

So adding a new value for a specific campaign means: open that campaign, jump to its Campaign Member Statuses related list, and modify the values there. Editing global picklist values for the Campaign object's Status field is the path for the broader campaign lifecycle picklist.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add the Campaign Member Statuses related list to the Page Layout.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Edit the picklist values for the Campaign Status in object Manager.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Mass modify the Campaign Member Statuses related list.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Modify the picklist value on the Campaign Member Statuses related list.

questions.text: Ursa Solar Major is evaluating Salesforce for its service team and would like to know what objects were available out of the box. Which three of the standard objects are available to an administrator considering a support use case? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
Out of the box, service teams generally rely on three standard objects: Account (the customer), Contract (the agreement that governs entitlement), and Case (the trackable issue). These three together cover the common service-cloud spine.

Ticket and Request are not standard Salesforce objects — they're terms from other systems. If you want to model them in Salesforce you create custom objects, but the question asks what's available out of the box.

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks has been asked to replace two old workflow rules that are doing simple field updates when a lead is created to improve processing time. What tool should the administrator use to replace the workflow rules?
questions.explanation:
Before-Save record-triggered flows are the modern, performant replacement for workflow rules that just update a field. Because they execute in the same DML as the save, they avoid the extra recursion and overhead a workflow field update would incur — measurably faster and Salesforce's recommended path forward.

Quick Action and Screen Flows require user interaction. Scheduled flows fire on a clock, not on record change. For a "lead is created → set fields" requirement, Before Save is the precise fit.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar uses Opportunity to track sales of solar energy products. The company has two separate sales teams that focus on different energy markets. The Services team also wants to use Opportunity to track installation. All three teams will need to use different fields and stages. How should the administrator configure this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Three teams with three different stages, three different sets of fields, and three different picklist values translates directly to: three sales processes (one per stage set), three record types (one per business model — they bind the right sales process and govern picklist values), and three page layouts (each tailored to the fields that matter for that team).

Skimping in any direction means compromising. One sales process can't model three stage flows; one page layout can't display three different field sets cleanly. The 3-3-3 build is what scales cleanly.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create three sales processes. Create three record types and one page layout.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create one sales process. Create three record types and three page layouts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create three sales processes. Create three record types and three page layouts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create one sales process. Create one record type and three page layouts.

questions.text: The service manager at Ursa Major Solar wants to let customers know that they have received their cases via email and their websites. Medium-priority and high-priority cases should receive different email notifications than low-priority cases. The administrator has created three email templates for this purpose. How should an administrator configure this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Auto-Response Rules send a templated email back to the submitter when a case (or lead) is created. You only get one Auto-Response Rule per object, but the rule itself can hold many rule entries — each with its own criteria, evaluation order, and email template.

So configure one rule for Case, then add three rule entries (low/medium/high priority) each pointing at the appropriate template. Three separate rules isn't possible (only one is active per object), and Workflow Rules don't filter the template by record-time criteria like Auto-Response can.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Include three assignment rules that fire when cases are created. Add a filter for case priority. Select the appropriate email template for each rule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add three auto-response rules. Configure one rule entry criteria for each rule and set a filter for case priority. Select the appropriate email template for each rule entry.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure one workflow rule that fires when cases are created. Add a filter for case priority. Select the appropriate email template for the rule.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create one auto-response rule. Configure three rule entry criteria and set a filter for case priority. Select the appropriate email template for each rule entry.

questions.text: The VP of sales at Dreamhouse Realty has requested a dashboard to visualize enterprise sales across the different teams. The key piece of data is the total of all sales for the year and the progress to the enterprise sales goal. What dashboard component will effectively show this number and the proximity to the total goal as a single value?
questions.explanation:
A Gauge component is purpose-built to show a single number against a target, with colored bands (red/yellow/green) signaling progress. That maps exactly to "total sales for the year + proximity to the goal".

A table is too dense for a single KPI; a stacked bar shows distribution; a donut shows part-to-whole shares. None of those communicate "how close to the goal" as cleanly as a gauge with band thresholds.

questions.text: A sales rep has left the company and an administrator has been asked to re-assign all their accounts and opportunities to a new sales rep and keep the teams as is. Which tool should an administrator use to accomplish this?
questions.explanation:
The Mass Transfer Records tool (Setup > Data Management) reassigns up to 250 records of the same type from one user to another in a single operation. Crucially, it preserves account/opportunity team membership, so re-pointing the owner doesn't blow away the collaborators.

Data Loader and Dataloader.io can also re-owner records but require careful CSV preparation and don't have the team-preservation toggle in their UI. Data Import Wizard is for inserts/updates of new data, not bulk owner changes. Mass Transfer is the lightest path here.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters has two different sales processes: one for business opportunities with four stages and one for partner opportunities with eight stages. Both processes will vary in page layouts and picklist value options. What should an administrator configure to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Different stage counts plus different page layouts and picklist values is the textbook scenario for record types layered on top of sales processes. Sales processes hold the stage list (4 stages vs 8 stages); record types bind the right sales process and offer different picklist values; the record type's page layout assignment finishes the job.

Validation rules can enforce data quality but can't show different picklists. Page layouts alone can't change picklist value sets. Public groups don't change object behavior. Record types + sales processes is the canonical answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Validation rules that ensure that users are entering accurate sales stage information.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Different page layouts that control the picklist values for the opportunity types.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Public groups to limit record types and sales processes for opportunities.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Separate record types and Sales processes for the different types of opportunities.

questions.text: An administrator installed a managed package that contains a permission set group. The permission set group includes Delete access on several objects, and the administrator needs to prevent users in the permission set group from being able to delete records. What should the administrator do to control Delete access?
questions.explanation:
A muting permission set sits inside a Permission Set Group and removes specific permissions that other members of the group grant. It's how you receive a managed package's permission set group but hold back select privileges (like Delete) that you don't want users to have.

Creating another permission set with Delete unchecked still leaves the group's Delete permission in effect — permissions are additive, you can't subtract by un-selecting. Roles and profile edits don't override what a permission set grants in the group. Muting is the only mechanism that actually removes a permission contributed by a group member.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use a muting permission set with a permission set group to mute selected permissions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a new permission set that has Delete access deselected for the objects.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a new role that prevents Delete permissions from rolling up to the users.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Edit the profile for the users to remove Delete access from the objects.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to calculate how much revenue has been generated for each of its marketing campaigns. How should an administrator deliver this information?
questions.explanation:
A Roll-Up Summary field, defined on the parent side of a master-detail relationship, aggregates child records into the parent (SUM, COUNT, MIN, MAX). Place it on Campaign with Opportunity as the source, filter on closed-won, and you get won revenue per campaign automatically.

A standard report is read-only and doesn't store the value back on the campaign. Periodic data jobs and workflow updates can simulate this but require maintenance and lag behind the source. Roll-up summary is real-time, declarative, and the right primitive.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Design a standard Campaign report and add the value Won Opportunities in Campaign field.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Perform periodic data job to update campaign records.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a roll-up summary field on Opportunity to Campaign.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a Total Value Field on campaign and use a workflow rule to update the value when an opportunity is won.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants to allow customers to create their own cases while visiting its public homepage. What should the administrator recommend?
questions.explanation:
Web-to-Case generates HTML you embed on a public page; visitors fill it in and a case is created in your org with the captured fields. It's the standard customer-self-serve path when you don't want to require a portal login.

Email-to-Case routes inbound email into cases and is great for support@ inboxes but doesn't give a public form on a homepage. Omni-Channel routes work to agents but doesn't capture cases from anonymous visitors. Web-to-Case is the precise fit.

questions.text: An administrator at Universal Containers needs a simple way to trigger an alert to the director of sales when opportunities reach an amount of $500,000. What should the administrator configure to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Big Deal Alerts (Setup > Forecasts) send an email to a designated user the moment an opportunity crosses a configured Amount and Probability threshold. They are simple, no-code, and exactly the "tell the director when a deal hits $X" pattern.

Update Reminders nudge owners about stale opportunities, not size. Kanban warning flags are visual cues for the rep, not email alerts to a director. The Key Deals component is a homepage widget, not a notification. Big Deal Alerts is built for this.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set up Big Deal Alerts for the amount.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Key Deals component on the homepage

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants users to only be able to choose Opportunity stage closed won if the Lead source has been selected. How should the administrator accomplish this goal?
questions.explanation:
Validation rules block the save when a formula evaluates to true, with an error tied to the field or top-of-page. The formula here checks: when StageName = 'Closed Won', LeadSource must not be blank. If both conditions are true the save is denied.

Making LeadSource a dependent picklist constrains values, not whether the parent has been set. Read-only or controlling-via-stage-only picklists don't enforce that LeadSource is filled. Validation rule is the precise enforcement mechanism for cross-field requirements at save time.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Make Lead Source a dependent picklist to the Opportunity stage field.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure a validation rule requiring Lead Source when the stage is set to closed won.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the Opportunity stage field to read only on the page layout.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Modify the Opportunity stage a dependent picklist to the Lead source field.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar wants to automatically notify a manager about any cases awaiting a response from an agent for more than 2 hours after case creation. Which feature should an administrator use to fulfill this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Case Escalation Rules trigger after a case sits in a target state for a configured time (e.g. unanswered for 2 hours since creation). Their actions can reassign the case, send email alerts, and/or change priority.

Assignment Rules fire on initial create, not after a wait period. Omni-Channel Supervisor is a monitoring console, not an automation. Formula fields can compute a stale flag but can't act on it. Escalation Rule is what closes the loop with email + reassignment.

questions.text: Sales users at Universal Containers are reporting that it is taking a long time to edit opportunity records. Normally, the only field they are editing is the Stage field. Which two options should the administrator recommend to help simplify the process? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
When all reps do is move records along a stage, the goal is to get to that field with as few clicks as possible. Path provides an inline stage tracker on the record page itself with key-fields editing in place. Kanban turns the list view into a drag-and-drop board where stage is the column.

Both eliminate the open-edit-save round trip for stage changes. Auto-launched flows still need to be triggered. A simplified page layout helps marginally but still requires opening a record. Path + Kanban is the precise UX answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a path for stage to the opportunity record page.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a Kanban list view for Opportunity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure an auto launched flow for Opportunity editing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a simplified Opportunity page layout.

questions.text: A sales rep has a list of 300 accounts with contacts that they want to load at one time. Which tool should the administrator utilize to import the records to Salesforce?
questions.explanation:
Data Import Wizard handles up to 50,000 records and walks the admin through column mapping with a friendly UI. For a 300-record batch it's the simplest, fastest path — no installation, no API knowledge required.

Data Loader and Dataloader.io scale higher (millions) but require setup and CSV-discipline. Manual import means typing them in. Data Import Wizard is sized exactly for this volume and is the recommended tool for under-50K loads.

questions.text: An administrator created a record trigger flow to update contacts. How should the administrator reference the values of the active record the flow is running on?
questions.explanation:
In a record-triggered flow, the special $Record global variable is bound to the record that fired the trigger — same idea as Apex's Trigger.new but in Flow. You read its fields with $Record.FieldName and it's available everywhere in the flow.

{!Contact.Id} or {!Account.Id} is generic Flow variable syntax but isn't auto-populated to the triggering record. Get Records would re-query the database for a record you already have. $Record is the cheap, idiomatic handle.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the Get Records element to find the Id.

questions.text: An administrator gets a rush request from Human Resources to remove a user's access to Salesforce immediately. The user is part of a hierarchy field called Direct Manager. What should the administrator do to fulfil the request?
questions.explanation:
Freeze on a user record is a fast, reversible "block sign-in immediately" lever — it doesn't free the license but it does cut access. That's exactly what the urgent HR ask needs while you do the slower cleanup of removing the user from hierarchy fields like Direct Manager.

Deactivation can fail or block when a user is referenced in required fields, and deletion is even harsher. Read-only profile changes still permit access. Freeze first, clean up references, then deactivate is the standard playbook.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Freeze the user to prevent them from logging in while removing them from being referenced in the Direct Manager field.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deactivate the user and delete any records where they are referenced in the Direct Manager field.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the user's profile to read-only while removing them from being referenced in the Direct Manager Field.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Delete the user and leave all records where they referenced in the Direct Manager Field without changes.

questions.text: AW Computing (AWC) occasionally works with independent contractors, who the company stores as Contacts in Salesforce. Contractors often change agencies, and AWC wants to maintain the historical accuracy of the record. What should AWC use to track Contacts?
questions.explanation:
Contacts to Multiple Accounts lets a single Contact record be linked to many Accounts via the AccountContactRelation junction. When a contractor moves to a new agency you simply add a new account relationship; the old one stays as history without spawning a duplicate contact.

Creating a new contact per agency loses the person's history. Junction objects work but reinvent what AccountContactRelation already does. Partner communities are about external login, not modeling. Contacts to Multiple Accounts is the built-in answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use a partner community to track the Contacts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a new Contact record for each agency.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a Junction object to track many-to-many relationship.

questions.text: Which two actions should an administrator perform with Case escalation rules? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Case Escalation Rule actions are scoped to: change the case owner (re-assign), notify someone (email alerts), and trigger workflow-style updates. They are designed to push a stuck case forward by moving it and announcing it.

Re-opening a closed case isn't an escalation action — closure is a status. Changing priority isn't part of the escalation action set either. Re-assign and Send Email Notifications are the two explicit options.

questions.text: The Sales director at Cloud Kicks wants to be able to predict upcoming revenue in the next several fiscal quarters so they can set goals and benchmark how reps are performing. Which two features should the administrator configure? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Forecasting (Collaborative Forecasts) projects future revenue from your pipeline. It needs structure to do that — and the structure comes from Opportunity Stages, which carry probability and forecast category. Configure both and you get rolled-up forecast numbers by quarter.

Sales Quotes are about formal pricing documents, not forecasting. Opportunity List Views show data but don't predict. Forecasting + Stages is the canonical pairing.

questions.text: Universal Containers requires a different Lightning page to be displayed when Accounts are viewed in the Sales Console and in the Service Console. How should an administrator meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Lightning record pages can be assigned as the default for an entire app. By creating two record pages for Account and assigning each as the app default in Sales Console and Service Console respectively, the same record renders differently depending on which app the user is in.

Page layouts and record types branch by profile/record type, not by app. Different profiles is overkill and can't model "same person, different app". App-default Lightning page assignment is the precise mechanism.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Assign Lightning pages as app default.

questions.text: Sales reps at Northern Trail Outfitters have asked for a way to change the Probability field value of their Opportunities. What should an administrator suggest to meet this request?
questions.explanation:
Probability is a standard percentage on Opportunity that's normally driven by the Stage. To let reps adjust it manually, just make the field editable on the page layout — Salesforce will respect their override.

Adding a stage doesn't allow editing the existing field. A new custom field is parallel data, not the same number. Forecasting feeds off Probability but doesn't make it editable. The page-layout property is the lightest fix.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Define a new Stage picklist value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a custom field on Opportunity.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Make the field editable on page layouts

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar has its business hours set from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM for the reps that are on pacific time. The reps on Eastern Time need business hours set to start 3 hours earlier to cover for support. How should an administrator solve for this issue?
questions.explanation:
Business Hours in Salesforce can be created as multiple records, each with its own time zone and weekly schedule. Assign one to each user (or use them on Cases via assignment) and reps see hours that make sense for their geography.

Adjusting the master entry to cover both windows confuses the data. Temporary hours don't address two sustained zones. Letting reps pick their own bypasses the org's controlled hours. One Business Hours record per zone is the right design.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set temporary business hours for each time zone.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adjust the current business hours to accommodate the Eastern Time Zone.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create one set of business hours per time zone.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Allow the reps to set business hours manually.

questions.text: An administrator at Cloud Kicks is building a flow that needs to search for records that meet certain conditions and store values from those records in variable for use later in the flow. What flow element should the administrator add?
questions.explanation:
Get Records is the Flow element that reads from the database — one record into a record variable, or many into a record-collection variable, optionally filtered. It is the read primitive in Flow.

Assignment moves data between variables you already have. Create/Update/Delete are write operations. When you need to "find records meeting criteria and use their fields later", Get Records is the answer.

questions.text: An administrator at Cloud Kicks has a flow in production that is supposed to create new records. However, no new records are being created. What could the issue be?
questions.explanation:
A flow has to be Active for it to fire on its trigger. If you build a flow in production but forget to switch the version to Active, no records will be created — even though the flow exists and its logic is correct.

Read-only flows don't exist as a concept. Flow URL deactivation isn't a thing here. Trigger missing would prevent saving. Inactive version is the most common cause of "no records being created", and the fix is a single click to activate.

questions.text: The sales manager at Cloud Kicks wants to set up a business process where opportunity discounts over 30% need to be approved by the VP of sales. Any discounts above 10% need to be approved by the user's manager. The administrator has been tasked with creating an approval process. Which are two considerations the administrator needs to review before setting up this approval process? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Discount isn't a standard field on Opportunity, so step one is to create a custom field that holds the value. Step two is to model the threshold logic — which is two distinct policies (over 30% to the VP, over 10% to the manager) and therefore two separate Approval Processes with different entry criteria and different approvers.

Manager standard field already exists — populating it is housekeeping, not a prerequisite for this design. Letting the submitter pick the approver bypasses the policy you're trying to enforce. Custom Discount field plus two approval processes is the right plan.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a custom Discount field on the opportunity to capture the discount amount

choices.label: B
choices.text: Populate the Manager standard field on the sales users' User Detail page.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Allow the submitter choose the approver manually.

questions.text: What are three characteristics of a master-detail relationship? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
Master-detail is a tight ownership relationship: the master can be a standard or custom object; the detail's owner and sharing are inherited from the master; deleting the master cascades to the detail; and roll-up summary fields are available on the master because the parent-child cardinality is fixed.

Permissions on the detail are NOT independent — they follow the master. Up to two master-detail relationships per object (not five) is the limit. The three correct attributes are master can be standard or custom, roll-ups are supported, and detail ownership inherits from master.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The master object can be a standard or custom object.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Permissions for the detail record are set independently of the master.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Each object can have up to five master-detail relationships.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Roll-up summaries are supported in master-detail relationships.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The owner field on the detail records is the owner of the master record.

questions.text: An administrator at Universal Containers has been asked to prevent users from accessing Salesforce from outside of their network. What are two considerations for this configuration? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Login IP Ranges can be set on a profile (the per-profile range) or on the org overall (Session Settings > Trusted IP Ranges). Together they define where users can sign in. To extend that enforcement to API calls (where browsers don't apply IP rules), you must turn on "Enforce Login IP Ranges on Every Request" in Session Settings.

Users can't change passwords to bypass IP. SSO doesn't ignore IP rules — those are enforced at Salesforce regardless of identity provider. The two operative considerations are profile/org IP rules and the every-request enforcement toggle.

choices.label: A
choices.text: IP address restrictions are set on the profile or globally for the org.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Users can change their password to avoid login IP restrictions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enforce Login IP Ranges on Every Request must be selected to enforce IP restrictions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Single sign-on will allow users to log in from anywhere.

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks has created an approval process for time off requests. Which two automated actions are available to be added as part of the approval process? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
The actions you can attach to an Approval Process step (or to initial submission, final approval, final rejection, recall) are: Field Update, Email Alert, Task, and Outbound Message. Field Update + Email Alert is the most common pair — set a status, notify the requester.

Chatter Post is not in that menu. Auto-launched Flows aren't directly attachable from the approval process action picker (you'd invoke them via Process/Flow). The two correct picks are Field Update and Email Alert.

questions.text: Which two capabilities are considerations when marking a field as required in Object Manager? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Marking a field "Required" in Object Manager makes it required everywhere a record is saved through the UI, and it shows up on every page layout for that object. But the API is a different door: SOAP/REST callers can still save without that field unless you also enforce it via validation rule or layout-level requirement. Web-to-Lead and Web-to-Case go through the API path, so they too can bypass the requirement.

So the two true considerations are: (a) the field is universally required in the UI, and (b) it is not required for API saves on that object.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The field is not required to save records via the API on that object.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The field is universally required to save a record on that object.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The field is added to every page layout on that object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The field is optional when saving records via web-to-lead and web-to-case

questions.text: Universal Containers requires that when an Opportunity is closed won, all other open opportunities on the same account must be marked as closed lost. Which automation solution should an administrator use to implement this request?
questions.explanation:
When closing one Opportunity should reach across to OTHER opportunities on the same Account and update them, you need automation that can query and update related records — Flow Builder. A record-triggered flow on Opportunity (after-save) can fetch the account's other open opportunities and bulk-update their stage to Closed Lost.

Quick Actions only act on the current record. Workflow Rules can't query and update sibling records this way. Outbound Message just sends a payload to an external endpoint. Flow is the only fit.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants a report to categorize accounts into small, medium, and large based on the dollar value found in the Contract Value Field. What feature should an administrator use to meet this request?
questions.explanation:
Bucket columns turn ranges of values (or sets of categorical values) into named groups inside a single report — without you having to add a new field to the object. Define small/medium/large bands on Contract Value, and the report gains a Size column you can group by.

Detail columns just show fields. Group Rows groups by an existing column but doesn't categorize by range. Filter Logic narrows what's shown but doesn't bucket. Bucket column is the no-code way to categorize on the fly.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks (CK) is partnering with a used shoe store and second-hand bicycle emporium. CK has an automated business process it wants to run once a week to count the number of open cases related to an account. How should the administrator recommend automating this business process?
questions.explanation:
Scheduled Flows run on a cadence (one-time, daily, weekly) and process a batch of records selected by their criteria. "Once a week, count open cases on each account, write the number back" is the canonical scheduled-flow pattern.

Workflow rules fire on record save, not on a clock. Process Builder doesn't have a true scheduled trigger. Edit-time processes don't capture the weekly cadence. Scheduled Flow in Flow Builder is the answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a workflow rule with an outbound message.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set up a scheduled process in Process Builder.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure a scheduled flow in flow Builder.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a process to update the account when it is edited

questions.text: An administrator has assigned a permission set group with the two-factor authentication for User Interface Logins permissions and the two-factor authentication for API Logins permission to a group of users. Which two prompts will happen when one of the users attempts to log in to Data Loader? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
When 2FA for both UI and API logins is enforced, a user logging into Data Loader (an API client) goes through verification. That means: (1) connecting an authenticator app to their Salesforce account so they hold a TOTP generator, and (2) entering the verification code (from email/SMS or the app, whichever is configured to deliver) at the prompt.

Reset My Security Token isn't a 2FA prompt — it's a separate self-service. "Download an authenticator app on mobile" is the user's responsibility but isn't itself a Salesforce-presented prompt. The two prompts the user actually sees are connect-an-authenticator and enter-the-code.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Users need to connect an authenticator app to their Salesforce account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Users need to get a security token from a trusted network using Reset My Security Token.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Users need to download and install an authenticator app on their mobile device.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Users need to enter a verification code from email or SMS, whichever has higher priority.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks need to be able to show different picklist values for sales and marketing users. Which two options will meet this requirement? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two valid combinations show different picklist values to different audiences. Record types route picklist values per record type, so one page layout can serve two record types each exposing a different value subset. Alternatively, profile-level picklist controls let two profiles see different values from a single record type's picklist.

Two layouts + one record type doesn't change the values; layouts don't filter picklists. Permission sets aren't a picklist-filter mechanism. Record-type + page-layout combos and profile-based picklist scoping are the correct two paths.

choices.label: A
choices.text: One page layout, two record types, one picklist

choices.label: B
choices.text: Two page layouts, one record type, two picklists

choices.label: C
choices.text: Two permission sets, one record type, one picklist

choices.label: D
choices.text: One record type, two profiles, one picklist

questions.text: At Universal Containers, users would like to be able to share Salesforce records with other members of their team, while collaborating around general topics as well. Which are two considerations for enabling this functionality? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Chatter Groups can be record-aware: you add the Records related list (or the Add Record action) to the group publisher and members can attach records right inside the group. Two configuration steps make this work — adding the Groups related list to the relevant object's page layouts, and configuring the Add Record action in the group publisher.

Groups aren't created automatically per department. Manually creating one group doesn't enable record sharing; the layout/publisher config is what does. Those two configurations are the prerequisites.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Collaboration groups are created automatically for every department.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Object layouts should be configured to include the groups related list.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Add Record action must be configured in the group publisher.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An administrator needs to create a group to enable record sharing

questions.text: Executives at Cloud Kicks have reported that their dashboards are showing inaccurate data. The administrator has discovered users are changing the source reports. Which two actions should the administrator take to preserve the integrity of the source reports? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Reports can live in folders with view-only access — recipients can run the report but can't change the underlying definition. Moving the dashboard's source reports into such a folder protects them from "helpful" edits that drift the dashboard's numbers.

Pairing that with creating a dedicated viewer-access folder gives a clean home for shared, locked-down sources. Personal/private folders hide reports entirely. Switching to dynamic dashboards changes whose security is applied but not whether the underlying reports can be edited.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a new report folder with viewer access.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Move the dashboard to the user's private folder.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move the dashboard reports to the view-only folder.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the dashboard to be a dynamic dashboard

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has decided to delete a custom field. What will happen to the data in the field when it is deleted?
questions.explanation:
Deleting a custom field doesn't immediately wipe the data. Salesforce holds the field and its values for ~15 days (often quoted as 20 in older material), giving you time to undelete and recover both the metadata and the data.

After that retention window the field and its data are permanently purged. The recycle bin is for records, not fields. The 15–20 day soft-delete window is what gives admins a safety net for accidental field deletions.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The data in the field is stored for 20 days.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The data associated with the field is required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The data is restorable from the recycle bin.

questions.text: AW Computing has six sales teams in a region. These teams always consist of the same account manager, engineer, and assistant. What should the administrator configure to make it easier for teams to collaborate with the same customer?
questions.explanation:
Account Teams are a built-in feature for tagging a small group of users with roles on an Account. Each user can also configure a Default Account Team — a list of teammates that gets applied automatically to every Account they own or create.

Opportunity Teams + splits are about deal credit, not account collaboration. A queue centralizes ownership but doesn't model role-per-person. Manual sharing scales poorly across six teams. Account Teams with a default team is exactly what fits.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable and configure standard opportunity teams with splits.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable account teams and show the users how to set up a default account team.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a queue for each team and assign account ownership to the queue.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Propose the users manually share all their accounts with their teammates.

questions.text: A user at Cloud Kicks is having issues logging in to Salesforce. The user asks the administrator to reset their password. Which two options should the administrator consider when resetting the user's password? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two genuinely useful behaviors apply when an admin resets a user's password. First, if the user was locked out from too many failed attempts, the password reset itself unlocks the account in one step. Second, after using the temporary password the user may be prompted for device activation (a code emailed to them) the first time they log in from that browser/device.

Resetting doesn't change the password policy itself. SSO users typically don't use the standard "Forgot Password" path. The two correct considerations are auto-unlock and device activation.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Resetting the password will change the user's password policy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Single sign-on users can reset their own passwords using the forgot password link.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Resetting a locked-out user's password automatically unlocks the user's account.

choices.label: D
choices.text: After resetting a password, the user may be required to activate their device to successfully log in to Salesforce.

questions.text: When users log in to Salesforce via the user interface, which two settings does the system check for authentication? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
When a user signs in to the Lightning UI, two profile-level settings gate the attempt: Login Hours (does this profile permit logins at this time?) and the Two-Factor Authentication for User Interface Logins permission (does the user need a verification code on top of the password?).

API-only 2FA permission applies to API logins, not UI. IP restrictions are profile or session settings, not on the role. Login Hours and 2FA-UI are the two operative checks for UI authentication.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The user's Two-Factor Authentication for API Logins permission

choices.label: C
choices.text: The user's profile login hours restrictions

choices.label: D
choices.text: The user's Two-Factor Authentication for User Interface Logins permission

questions.text: Which two solutions could an administrator find on the AppExchange to enhance their organization? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
The AppExchange marketplace exposes apps and components you can install, plus a directory of certified consultants who can be engaged for projects. Both extend the org's capabilities — components add functionality, consultants add expertise.

Communities and Customers aren't AppExchange categories. The two valid categories the question is testing are consultants and components.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters has requested that when the Referral Date field is updated on the custom object Referral Source, the parent object Referral also needs to be updated. Which automation solution should an administrator use to meet this request?
questions.explanation:
Process Builder can fire on a child record save and update fields on the parent (it can update related records via a lookup). When the Referral Date changes on Referral Source, a process can locate the parent Referral and roll the date up.

Workflow Field Update can update fields, but only on the same record (or master, in master-detail) — limited cross-object reach. Approval Process is review-oriented. Lightning Web Components are UI building blocks, not automations. Process Builder is the right tool for cross-object child→parent updates without code.

questions.text: Sales and Customer Care at Ursa Major Solar need to see different fields on the Case related list from the Account record. Sales users want to see Case created date and status while Customer Care would like to see owner, status, and contact. What should the administrator use to achieve this?
questions.explanation:
The Page Layout Editor's Related Lists section lets you customize which columns appear on a related list, including their order and how the list is sorted. Different layouts can show different columns, so Sales sees Created Date + Status while Customer Care sees Owner + Status + Contact.

Related Lookup Filters control which records are eligible — not which columns show. Compact and Search Layout Editors apply elsewhere. Page Layout Editor is the precise lever for "different columns on the same related list".

questions.text: The support manager at Cloud Kicks wants to respond to customers as quickly as possible. They have requested that the response include the top five troubleshooting tips that could help solve the customer's issue. What should the administrator suggest to meet these requirements?
questions.explanation:
Salesforce Knowledge is the structured article system designed for exactly this — authored articles (FAQs, troubleshooting steps, procedures) with data categories, versioning, and inline insertion into emails or case feeds. Top-N article suggestions then surface relevant articles next to a case.

Auto-Response Rules send the same message; Email Alerts are notifications, not knowledge content; Assignment Rules route cases. Knowledge Articles are the right primitive for sharing curated answers.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters is using one profile for all of its marketing users, providing read-only access to the Campaign object. A few marketing users now require comprehensive edit access on Campaigns. How should an administrator fulfil this request?
questions.explanation:
Permission Sets grant additional access on top of a profile without forcing you to clone the profile. For "a few users need edit on Campaigns while everyone else stays read-only", create a permission set with Edit on Campaign and assign it to the few people who need it.

Org-wide defaults work at the record level, not the object/CRUD level. The Marketing User checkbox is a feature flag for campaign management, not the campaign-edit permission gate. Field-level security is finer than object access. Permission set is the right tool.

questions.text: The administrator for Cloud Kicks has created a screen flow to help service reps ask the same set of questions when customers call in with issues. This screen should be visible from cases. How should the screen flow be distributed?
questions.explanation:
A Lightning record page (built in Lightning App Builder) is the native home for a flow component. Drop the Flow component on the Case record page and select your screen flow — agents now have it inline whenever they're working a case.

Page Layouts don't carry Lightning components. Component Filter is a property on a component, not a delivery vehicle. Home page would put it everywhere. The Case Lightning record page is the precise placement.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters has a custom quick action on Account that creates a new Case. How should an administrator make the quick action available on the Salesforce mobile app?
questions.explanation:
Each page layout has a "Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions" section. Drag the quick action there and it appears in the action bar on the Account record both in Lightning and in the Salesforce mobile app.

The compact layout controls the highlights panel, not actions. The mobile navigation menu adds tabs, not record-level actions. A custom Lightning App is overkill. The mobile/lightning actions section is the precise placement.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a custom Lightning App with the action.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Modify compact Case page layout to include the action.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Include the action in the Salesforce Mobile Navigation menu.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience action to the page layout.

questions.text: The administrator at DreamHouse Realty added an email quick action to the Case page layout and is unable to see the action on the case feed. Which feature must be enabled to ensure the quick action will be displayed as expected?
questions.explanation:
Email-to-Case is the feature that powers the case-feed email tooling. Quick action authoring in the layout is one half; the other half is enabling Email-to-Case in setup so the system has the routing and threading pieces wired up to actually send mail from the feed.

Email Notifications, Email Alerts, and Email Templates don't enable the feed-side action. Turning Email-to-Case on is what makes the email quick action functional in the case feed.

questions.text: An administrator has reviewed an upcoming critical update. How should the administrator proceed with activation of the critical update?
questions.explanation:
Critical Updates are platform behavior changes Salesforce will eventually flip on for everyone. The right move when you see one queued is to activate it in a sandbox first, run your customizations and integrations against the new behavior, fix anything that breaks, and only then activate (or let it auto-activate) in production.

Letting it auto-activate untested can break flows or Apex. Sandboxes are exactly the safe place to validate. The "test in sandbox first" pattern is the recommended approach.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Activate the critical update in a sandbox.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Allow the critical update to auto-activate.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Activate the critical update in production.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Allow the critical update to auto-activate in a sandbox.

questions.text: DreamHouse Realty regularly processes customer requests for warranty work and would like to offer customers a self-serve option to generate cases. Which two solutions should an administrator use to meet this request? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two parallel self-service paths exist: Web-to-Case (a HTML form generator you embed on a public page) and Email-to-Case (point a support@ inbox at your org and inbound mail becomes cases). Customers pick whichever channel suits them; both create cases automatically.

Case Escalation routes already-existing cases. Case Queues are containers, not capture points. Web-to-Case + Email-to-Case is the canonical pair for self-service case capture.

questions.text: An administrator is on a tight deadline to create dashboards for the sales and marketing teams at AW Computing. What should the administrator do to meet the deadline without increasing the budget?
questions.explanation:
The AppExchange has thousands of pre-built solutions, many free, that drop into your org. For dashboard packs in particular there are well-rated free or low-cost packages that get you 80% of the way and let you tweak the last 20%. That's the budget-friendly path that beats hand-building under deadline.

Training is slow. A consultant costs money. Manual build burns the deadline. AppExchange first, customize second is the right play.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Train someone on the sales and marketing teams to build dashboards.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Check the AppExchange for prebuilt Solution that can be easily customized.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hire a Consultant to build the custom dashboards.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Build the dashboards manually to meet the deadline.

questions.text: Dreamhouse realty wants to offer a form on its experience cloud site where inspectors will submit findings from a property inspection. Which feature should an administrator place on the page to fulfill this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A Screen Flow embedded on an Experience Cloud page is the standard way to capture inputs from external users (inspectors here). The flow renders forms, validates input, and writes records on submit.

Related List shows existing data. Autolaunched Flow has no UI. Record Detail just displays a record. Screen Flow is the only option that presents a form for the inspector to fill in.

questions.text: The administrator at Ursa Major Solar needs to make sure the unassigned cases from VIP customers get transferred to the appropriate service representative within 5 hours. VIP Customers have access to support 24 hours a day. How should this be configured?
questions.explanation:
Escalation Rules can fire after a configurable wait, ignoring or honoring business hours, and one of their primary actions is to reassign the case to a different user or queue. Pointed at "unassigned VIP cases older than 5 hours" with no business-hours filter (because VIPs get 24/7 support), they reassign and notify automatically.

Assignment Rules fire on save, not after a wait. Business Hours by themselves don't escalate. Case Queues are destinations. Escalation Rule is the active driver.

questions.text: An administrator at Ursa Major Solar needs to send information to an external accounting system. What workflow action should the administrator use to accomplish this?
questions.explanation:
Outbound Message is the workflow action that POSTs a SOAP message to an endpoint URL — designed exactly for telling another system "this happened, here are the fields". For "Salesforce → external accounting", it's the canonical no-code path.

Assign Task creates a Salesforce task. Create Record stays inside the org. Custom Notification is a UI toast for Salesforce users. Outbound Message is the only option that delivers data outbound.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters has the Case Object set to private. The support manager raised a concern that reps have a broader view of data than expected and can see all cases on their groups dashboards. What could be causing reps to have inappropriate access to data on dashboards?
questions.explanation:
Dashboards have a "running user" — the security context whose visibility determines the data the dashboard shows. Dynamic Dashboards let the running user be the viewing user (or chosen from a list), so each viewer sees only what their access allows. If reps see all cases on a dashboard despite a private model, the dashboard is dynamic with a high-privilege running user.

Dashboard Filters and Subscriptions don't change visibility. Public Dashboards control sharing of the dashboard itself, not the data. Dynamic Dashboards is the relevant lever.

questions.text: An administrator wants to trigger a follow-up task for the opportunity owner when they close an opportunity as won and another task after 60 days to check in with the customer. Which two automation tools should the administrator use? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
A two-step ask: act now (create a follow-up task on close) and act later (another check-in 60 days out). Process Builder handles the immediate trigger nicely. The 60-day check-in needs a future-dated step; modeling it via a date Field Update plus a time-dependent workflow rule (or scheduled actions) is the no-code way.

Workflow Rule alone doesn't run on close-won as cleanly as Process Builder. Outbound Message is integration plumbing. Process Builder + Field Update covers the immediate-and-future combination cleanly.

questions.text: An administrator creates a custom text area field on the Account object and adds it to the service team's page layout. The services team manager loves the addition of this field and wants it to appear in the highlights panel so that the services reps can quickly find it when on the Account Page. How should the administrator accomplish this?
questions.explanation:
Compact Layouts control which fields appear in the highlights panel on Lightning record pages and in the Salesforce mobile app's record headers. Defining a custom compact layout in Object Manager > Account > Compact Layouts is how you surface a field "up top" without changing the rest of the page.

Page Layouts and the highlights "panel" are governed by the compact layout, not by the page layout sections. Required fields and reordering don't promote a field to the highlights panel. Compact Layouts is the precise lever.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a new page layout and a new section titled highlights panel.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In the Account object manager, create a custom compact layout.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From the page layout editor, drag the field to the highlights panel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Make the field required and move it to the top of the page.

questions.text: A team of support users at Cloud Kicks is helping inside sales reps make follow-up calls to prospects that filled out an interest form online. The team currently does not access the lead object. How should an administrator provide proper access?
questions.explanation:
Permission Sets are the recommended way to extend access without forking profiles. Build a permission set that grants Lead object access (read/edit/create as appropriate) and assign it to the support users who need to make follow-up calls. The base profile stays untouched.

A new profile is heavier and creates maintenance debt. Roles affect record sharing, not object access. Manual sharing is per-record. Permission Set is the smallest, cleanest grant.

questions.text: An administrator supporting a global team of Salesforce users has been asked to configure company settings. (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Company Information settings include locale, language, currency, fiscal year, and other org-wide defaults. For a global team, the two settings most directly impacting daily display are Currency Locale (formats and currencies in reports/records) and Default Language (labels and UI text for users who haven't overridden it).

Login Hours and Password Policy are security/profile settings rather than company-wide locale settings. Currency Locale and Default Language are the right knobs for global usability.

questions.text: Which item is available in a Lightning App where visibility is limited to the Salesforce Mobile App?
questions.explanation:
The Utility Bar (configured per Lightning App) is a docked bar at the bottom of the screen with quick-access tools — notes, history, custom utilities. It's a Lightning desktop concept that does NOT show on the Salesforce mobile app.

Today, Favorites, and Home Page all exist on mobile in some form. Utility Bar is the desktop-only Lightning App feature, which fits "available in a Lightning App where visibility is limited to NOT the mobile app" framing.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar wants to know which of its marketing efforts are helping the team win Opportunities. What should an administrator configure to provide these insights?
questions.explanation:
Campaign Influence is the Salesforce feature that attributes opportunity revenue back to the campaigns that touched it. With it enabled and an attribution model selected, you can report on which campaigns are actually driving wins.

Campaign Hierarchy organizes campaigns into a tree (useful for rollups) but doesn't compute influence. Mapping lead fields and tracking list emails are tangential. Campaign Influence is the right feature for "which marketing efforts are winning deals".

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar uses two different page layouts for Account records. One page layout reflects the fields related to customer accounts and another page layout includes fields for partner accounts. What should the administrator configure to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Two distinct kinds of Account record (customer vs partner) with two different page layouts is the textbook case for Record Types. Each type binds the appropriate page layout via the record-type-to-layout assignment per profile.

Sharing rules and account teams don't switch the layout. Object-level permission grants don't differentiate by record. Record Types is the canonical answer for "two flavors of the same object that should look different".

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use a public group and a criteria-based sharing rule to share customer accounts with the partner team.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add members of the partner management team to the default Account team for the customer accounts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Grant create, read, edit and delete access to customer accounts on the partner team profile.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create one record type for customer accounts and one record type for partner accounts.

questions.text: Users at Cloud Kicks want to see information more useful for their role on the Case page. How should an administrator make the pages more dynamic and easier to use?
questions.explanation:
Component Visibility filters on a Lightning record page show or hide a component based on field values, role, profile, or device. The result is a single record page that adapts — different agents see different relevant components based on case fields without separate pages.

Removing fields or deleting components affects everyone. Tab components organize but don't conditionally hide. Component Visibility filters give the precise role-based dynamism.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add Component visibility filters to the Components.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remove fields from the record details component.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Delete the extra component from the page.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Include more tab components with filters.

questions.text: Universal Containers (UC) customers have provided feedback that their support cases are not being responded to quickly enough. UC wants to send all unassigned Cases that have been open for more than 2 hours to an urgent Case queue and alert the support manager. Which feature should an administrator configure to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Case Escalation Rules with a 2-hour timer escalate stale cases — they can change owner (push to an urgent queue) and fire an email alert (notify the support manager). That single rule covers both the routing and the alerting in one go.

Scheduled Reports notify on a schedule, not on a per-case threshold. Dashboard Refreshes don't act. Assignment Rules fire on create. Case Escalation Rules are the unique fit for time-based, per-case escalation with notification.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has created a screen flow for their sales team to use when they add new leads. The screen flow collects name, email and shoe preference. Which two things should the administrator do to display the screen flow? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
A screen flow needs a host — a place users can reach it. Two clean placement options: create a Tab pointing at the screen flow (gives it a top-level navigation entry), or drop a Flow component on a record/home Lightning page (puts it inline where it's contextual).

Utility bar isn't designed for forms. AppExchange installs are unrelated to surfacing your own flow. Tab + Flow component on a Lightning page are the canonical placements.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a tab and add the screen flow to the page.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a flow element and add the screen flow to the record page.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add the flow in the utility bar of the console

choices.label: D
choices.text: Install an app from the AppExchange

questions.text: Universal Containers has two sales teams, Sales team A and Sales team B. Each team has their own role in the role hierarchy. Both roles are subordinates of the same Manager role. How should the administrator share records owned by sales team A with Sales team B?
questions.explanation:
When the standard sharing primitives (role hierarchy, sharing rules, criteria) don't model an ad-hoc need, Manual Sharing fills the gap. Owners can share a specific record with another user or group as a one-off.

Hierarchical sharing requires Team B to be above Team A — they're peers here. Criteria-based sharing rules act on field values, not arbitrary "share these specific records". Manual sharing is the appropriate one-off mechanism.

questions.text: An administrator at Cloud Kicks needs to export a file of closed won opportunities from the last 90 days. The file should include the Opportunity Name, ID, Close Date, and Amount. How should the administrator export this file?
questions.explanation:
The Data Export Service (Setup > Data Management > Data Export) lets admins export selected objects to CSV files in a zip — a simple, self-service path for "give me Opportunities with these fields". You can also schedule it for backup purposes.

Data Import Wizard is the inverse direction. Data Loader is more powerful but requires installation and setup. For a one-off targeted export, the in-setup tool is fastest.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters wants emails received from customers to generate cases automatically. How should the administrator ensure that the emails are sent to the correct queue?
questions.explanation:
Email-to-Case has a routing-address feature: every routing address can be configured to deliver into a specific Case Queue. Inbound mail to a particular alias creates the case directly in that queue, no flow required.

A flow could do the routing but is overkill. Custom Apex email service requires code. Escalation Rules act after creation, not at intake. Email-to-Case routing addresses are the built-in solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Utilize a flow to identify the correct queue and assign the case.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use a custom email service to set the owner of the case upon creation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create an Escalation Rule to send cases to the correct queue.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure Email-to-Case so emails are delivered to the correct queue

questions.text: Sales reps at Cloud Kicks want to be notified when they have a high likelihood of winning an opportunity over $1,000,000. Which feature meets this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Big Deal Alerts (Forecast settings) email a designated user when an opportunity reaches a configured Amount and Probability. "Notify me on opportunities over $1M with high likelihood" is exactly that pattern.

Key Deals is a homepage component, not a notifier. Activity Timeline displays history. Performance chart visualizes the rep's pipeline. Big Deal Alerts is the only one that proactively notifies on threshold.
