questions.text: Universal Containers wants to increase the security of their org by requiring stricter user passwords. Which two of the following should an administrator configure? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
The most direct password-strength controls are Minimum Password Length and Password Complexity Requirements (must include letter, number, special char, etc.). Both are configured under Setup > Password Policies.

"Different than username" and "prevent common words" are good practices but not direct password-policy toggles in Salesforce. Length and complexity are the two real settings.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to know the average stage duration for all closed Opportunities. How should an administrator support this request?
questions.explanation:
Salesforce ships a standard report called Opportunity Stage Duration that, for each closed opportunity, computes how long it spent in each stage. Group by stage, summarize the duration column, and the average pops out — no custom build required.

Process Builder/formula fields can derive the stage time per record but require maintenance and don't aggregate by themselves. Reporting snapshots layer on top. The standard report is the smallest path.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use process builder to capture the daily average on each opportunity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add Formula Fields to track Stages on each Opportunity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Run the Opportunity Stage Duration report.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refresh weekly reporting snapshots for Closed Opportunities.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar has a path on Case. The Company wants to require its users to follow the status values as they are on the path. Agents should be prohibited from reverting the case back to a previous status. Which feature should an administrator use to fulfill this request?
questions.explanation:
Path is a visual stage tracker — it doesn't enforce direction. To prevent backsliding (e.g. moving Case status from Closed back to Open), pair the Path with a validation rule that blocks the save when the new status is "earlier" than the prior status. The rule uses ISCHANGED() and PRIORVALUE() to check direction.

Global Value Sets and Predefined Field Values populate values, not prevent transitions. Dependent Picklists filter values, not order. Validation Rule is the only one that can block illegal transitions.

questions.text: Sales reps miss key fields when filling out an opportunity record through the process. Reps need to move forward but are unable to enter previous stage. Which three options should the administrator use to address this need? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
Path with Guided Selling shows reps the right fields and tips at each stage — reducing "what should I fill in?" confusion. Validation Rules can require fields at specific stages so the rep can't slide forward without the data. And marking fields required on the page layout enforces them at save time too.

Path itself surfaces fields but doesn't make them required. A flow can collect data on demand but doesn't gate the save. Guided selling + validation rules + page-layout required fields together cover the "must enter X before moving on" scenario.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Flow to mark fields required.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Mark fields required on the page layout.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks (CK) has a new administrator who is asked to put together a memo detailing Salesforce uses to budget for upcoming license purchases. Where should the administrator go to find out what type of licenses CK has purchased and how many are available?
questions.explanation:
The User Licenses related list on Setup > Company Information shows every license type the org has purchased, how many are total, used, and remaining. That's exactly what an admin needs for a license-purchase budget memo.

Searching for license types in setup explains them but doesn't show counts. User Management is for individual users. Usage-Based Entitlements covers things like sandbox refreshes, not user licenses. Company Information's User Licenses related list is the answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Search for licenses types in setup.

choices.label: B
choices.text: User Licenses Related List in Company information.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Usage based entitlement related list in company information.

questions.text: The marketing team at Ursa Major Solar wants to send a personalized email whenever a lead fills out the web-to-Lead form on their website. They want to send different messages based on the Lead Industry Field Value. What should an administrator configure to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Auto-Response Rules can branch by field value via multiple rule entries — each entry has criteria and its own email template. Filtering by Lead.Industry on each entry lets you send a tailored welcome email per industry whenever the web form posts a new lead.

Validation rules block saves; they can't send emails. Process Builder + email alerts could work but is heavier. Assignment rules with email alerts notify owners, not leads. Auto-Response Rule is the precise feature for "email the new lead with industry-specific content".

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use Validation rule to trigger workflow to email to Lead.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure an auto response rule to email the lead.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a public group and process builder to email the lead.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an assignment rule to email the lead

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has a Customer success agent going on leave and needs to change ownership on multiple cases. Which two users are able to fulfill this request? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two roles can change ownership on multiple cases: a user above the case owner in the role hierarchy (managers see and reassign their team's records), and any System Administrator (whose profile grants modify-all). Both are legitimate paths.

Read access on Account doesn't grant case write. The "Manage Cases" permission isn't a standard Salesforce permission name. Manager role + System Administrator profile are the two valid actors.

choices.label: A
choices.text: A user with Read Permission on account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A user with manager role above the agent.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A user with the System Administrator profile.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A user with the Manage Cases Permission

questions.text: The marketing director at Northern Trail Outfitters has requested that the budget field is populated in order for the Lead Status field to be marked as qualified. What tool should the administrator use to fulfill this request?
questions.explanation:
A validation rule with the formula AND(ISPICKVAL(Status,'Qualified'), ISBLANK(Budget)) blocks the save until Budget is filled when status moves to Qualified. That enforces the policy at exactly the right transition.

Lead Conversion happens later in the lifecycle. Required Field at the layout level requires it always. Workflow Rule can update or notify but not block save. Validation Rule is the precise enforcement.

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks created a new field for tracking returns on their new cloud shoe. A user has submitted a case to the administrator indicating that the new field is unavailable. Which two steps should an administrator do to troubleshoot this issue? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
If a user can't see a new field on a record, the two universal causes are: the field-level security hides it for that profile/permission set, and/or the page layout assigned to that profile doesn't include the field. Verify both.

Setup Audit Trail tracks changes made; it doesn't reveal why a field is invisible. Org-wide defaults govern record sharing, not field visibility. Page Layout + Field-Level Security are the right two checkpoints.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ensure that the page layout for the user's profile has been updated.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run the setup audit trail for the organization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Update the organization wide default for the object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Review the field level security of the field for the user profile

questions.text: The administrator at Ursa Major Solar has created a new record type for customer warranty cases. Which two assignments should the administrator use to display the new record type to users? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Showing a record type to users requires two assignments: the user's profile must have the record type marked available (Profile Assignment), and a page layout must be assigned for that profile + record type combination (Page Layout Assignment).

Roles affect record visibility, not record type availability. App Manager governs apps and tabs. Profile + Page Layout assignments are the two needed steps.

questions.text: A new Sales Rep at Ursa Major has a qualified lead that is ready for conversion. When using the Lead Conversion process, which two records can be created? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Lead Conversion creates an Account, a Contact, and optionally an Opportunity. Account and Contact are always created (or matched), so they are the two definite creations from the conversion process.

Campaign and Case are not lead-conversion outputs. Campaign membership is preserved, not created. Case is unrelated to lead conversion.

questions.text: Universal Containers (UC) has a queue that is used for managing tasks that need to be worked by the UC customer support team. The same team will now be working some of UC's Cases. Which two options should the administrator use to help the support team? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two configuration steps adapt the existing queue: enable Case as an available object on the queue (otherwise it accepts only its current object types), and use Case Assignment Rules to route the right cases to that queue.

Configuring a flow is more work than needed. Creating a new queue is unnecessary when the existing one can be extended. Add Case as available + assignment rule are the two minimal steps.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure a flow to assign the cases to the queue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use assignment rules to set the queue as the owner of the case.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add Case to the existing queue as an available object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a new queue and add Cases as an available object.

questions.text: The administrator at AW Computing wants to send off client welcome tasks and a welcome email to the primary contact automatically when an Opportunity is Closed Won. What automation tool best accomplishes this?
questions.explanation:
Process Builder fires on close-won and creates a Task (welcome task) and an Email Alert (welcome email). Both actions are first-class in Process Builder, so the whole "celebrate the win and onboard the customer" sequence is one process with two actions.

Validation rules block saves; outbound messages call external systems; approval processes drive review. None send a welcome email + create a task automatically the way Process Builder does.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks users are seeing error messages when they use one of their screen flows. The error messages are confusing but could be resolved if the users entered more information on the account before starting the flow. How should the administrator address this issue?
questions.explanation:
Flow's Fault connector branches on element failure. From a failed Create/Update Records, route to a screen that explains what happened and what fields the user needs to fix — much friendlier than a raw stack trace.

Removing validation rules makes data quality worse. Permission sets to bypass errors hide problems. Disabling the end-user error message removes context without giving guidance. Fault connector + a friendly screen is the right pattern.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Remove validation rules so that the users are able to process without complete records.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a permission set to allow users to bypass the error.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a fault connector and display a screen with text explaining what went wrong and how to correct it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Uncheck the end user Flow Errors box in setup.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has a custom object named Shoe. The administrator has been asked to ensure that when a relationship is created between Account and Shoe to prevent orphaned shoe records. What should the administrator do to complete this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A master-detail relationship makes the parent the owner: deleting the parent cascades to children, so children can never become orphans. That matches the "shoes belong to an account; if account is deleted, shoes go too" requirement.

Wait — re-read: the requirement says "prevent orphaned shoe records" which a master-detail solves by making the relationship required and parent-owned. Indirect, encrypted, and hierarchical lookups serve other purposes (external IDs, encryption, user hierarchies). Master-detail is the right type.

questions.text: AW Computing needs to capture a loss reason in a rich text field when an opportunity is Closed Lost. How should an administrator configure this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A validation rule with formula AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName,'Closed Lost'), ISBLANK(Loss_Reason__c)) blocks the save until Loss Reason is provided once the rep marks the deal lost. The rule is targeted to that exact state — open deals don't need a loss reason.

Required-on-layout makes it always required, even on open deals. Object-level required is the same problem. Workflow Rule can't block saves. Validation Rule is the targeted enforcement.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Select the requirement checkbox next to the loss reason field on the page layout.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a validation rule to display an error if stage is Closed lost and Loss Reason is blank.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Check the required checkbox on the Loss Reason field in Object Manager.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure a workflow rule to display an error if Loss Reason is blank

questions.text: Users at Cloud Kicks want to be able to create a task that will repeat every two weeks. What should an administrator do to meet the requirement?
questions.explanation:
Activity Settings has a checkbox to "Enable Creation of Recurring Tasks". Until that is on, users see no option to schedule a task that repeats on a cadence — once enabled, the task creation UI gains the recurrence options (frequency, end date).

Flow and workflow can create future-dated single tasks but don't expose the native recurrence series. The standalone "Recurring Activities" toggle is for events. The right answer is the Activity Settings recurring-tasks checkbox.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable Creation of Recurring Tasks in Activity Settings

choices.label: C
choices.text: Workflow rule to create recurring tasks.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants its reports to show a Fiscal Year that starts on February 1 and has 12 months. How should the administrator address this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Salesforce supports two fiscal year shapes: Standard (12 months, configurable starting month) and Custom (define quarters/periods explicitly). For "starts February 1, 12 months", the Standard year with a starting month of February is the simplest match — it preserves a normal monthly cadence offset from January.

Custom fiscal years are for organizations with non-standard period definitions (4-4-5, 13-period, etc.) and add complexity you don't need here. Standard with February as the start month is the right setting.

Note: depending on org configuration, "Custom" may be required to choose any non-January start. Refer to the org's Fiscal Year setup for the exact menu.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the Fiscal Year to Custom and the starting month as February.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the Fiscal Year to Custom and the duration to 4 quarters.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set the Fiscal Year to Standard and the starting month as February.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set the Fiscal Year to Standard and the duration to 12 months.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has asked the administrator to test a new screen flow that creates contacts. What are two key components of testing the flow? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two complementary testing approaches exist for a screen flow that creates contacts. First, run the flow itself in a sandbox/playground and create real contacts to confirm end-to-end behavior. Second, use Flow Builder's Debug feature, which lets you supply input values, step through elements, and inspect the values and decisions at each point.

A "flow interview" is what fires when the flow runs — not a separate testing artifact. Sandbox is a good place to test, but the question pairs running and debugging as the two key components.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set up a flow interview to test the flow.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Run the flow using it to create contacts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use Debug to test the flow in Flow Builder.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Test the flow in a sandbox.

questions.text: An administrator at Universal Containers is reviewing current security settings in the company's Salesforce org. What should the administrator do to prevent unauthorized access to Salesforce?
questions.explanation:
Multi-Factor Authentication is the single biggest defense against credential-based attacks: even with a stolen password, an attacker can't log in without the second factor. Salesforce strongly encourages (and increasingly requires) MFA for production logins.

Disabling TLS or expanding org-wide defaults weakens security. Caching/autocomplete on the login page is irrelevant. Enabling MFA is the highest-leverage action to prevent unauthorized access.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Enable caching and autocomplete on login page

questions.text: An administrator needs to store the ID of a record type for later use in a flow. Which kind of variable should the administrator use?
questions.explanation:
The ID variable type stores a 15- or 18-character Salesforce record ID. When you need to remember which record type to use later in the flow (e.g., to assign to a record on Create), an ID variable is the precise type.

Boolean stores true/false; text stores arbitrary text; record stores a full record object. ID is the targeted type for storing just a record's ID.

questions.text: Universal Containers (UC) would like to count the number of open cases associated with each account and update the account with this value every Friday evening. UC has several hundred open cases at any given time. What should the administrator use to complete this request?
questions.explanation:
Scheduled Flows run on a configured cadence (daily, weekly, monthly) and process a batch of records you select. "Every Friday evening, count open cases per Account, write the result back to the Account" is the canonical use case for a scheduled flow.

Record-triggered flows fire on save. Scheduled Process Builder isn't a real feature. Roll-up summary is real-time but only works on master-detail. Scheduled flow is the right pattern for time-driven aggregations across hundreds of accounts.

questions.text: The business development team at Cloud Kicks thinks the account creation process has too many fields to fill out and the page feels cluttered. They have requested the administrator to simplify the process. Which automation tool should an administrator use?
questions.explanation:
Flow Builder Screen Flows can present a streamlined wizard with only the essential fields, hiding everything else and walking the user step-by-step. That's a much cleaner UX than a cluttered standard create page when only a few fields actually matter.

Approval Process is for review, not data entry. Workflow Rule has no UI. Validation Rule blocks saves but doesn't simplify entry. Flow Builder is the right tool for "make this entry experience easier".

questions.text: What should an administrator use as an identifier when importing and updating records from a separate financial system?
questions.explanation:
An External ID is a custom field flagged as the upsert/match key with values that come from another system. When importing or updating from that external system you specify the External ID column and Salesforce upserts on it — no need to know Salesforce IDs.

Auto-Number generates internal sequential IDs you can't pre-populate from outside. Rich Text and Record ID are unrelated. External ID is the standard mechanism for cross-system record matching.

questions.text: DreamHouse Realty has an approval process. A manager attempts to approve the record but receives an error. What should an administrator review to troubleshoot this request?
questions.explanation:
When an approver gets an error, a common cause is that the next approver step in the chain points to a user who is inactive or no longer exists. The approval can't progress because the destination is invalid.

A delegated approver only matters if the approver is unavailable. Field-level security and page layouts don't cause approval-routing errors. Verifying the next approver is active is the first step to troubleshoot a stuck approval.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a delegated approver for the next approver in the process.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Update the field level security to view on fields that are updated in the process.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Check if the user in the next approver is inactive or missing

choices.label: D
choices.text: Review the page layout to ensure, the fields updated in the process are visible

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants to try out an app from the AppExchange to ensure that the app meets its needs. Which two options should the administrator suggest? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two safe ways to evaluate an AppExchange app exist: download into a Trailhead Playground (a free, isolated learning org with full functionality and no real data), or install in a sandbox (a copy of production for testing). Both let you exercise the app's behavior without risk to production.

Test Drive in production is risky. Edition compatibility is something to check on the listing, not a way to "try" the app. Trailhead Playground + sandbox are the two safe trial environments.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Test Drive in a production org.

questions.text: Which three aspects of standard fields should an administrator customize? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
Standard fields aren't field-locked the way they sometimes seem. You can edit Picklist Values (add/remove/reorder), Help Text (the inline tooltip the user sees), and Decimal Places on numeric standard fields where applicable. Each is configurable in Object Manager.

Field history tracking exists but is a separate enable; field name is the API name (typically not changed for standards). Picklist values, help text, and decimal places are three legitimate, common standard-field customizations.

questions.text: Which tool should an administrator use to review recent configuration changes made in their org?
questions.explanation:
Setup Audit Trail logs every metadata-level change in Setup — who changed it, when, and what. It retains 180 days of changes by default, downloadable as CSV.

Critical Updates lists upcoming platform changes, not changes you made. Debug Logs capture per-transaction execution, not setup changes. Field History Tracking captures field value changes on records. Setup Audit Trail is the precise tool for "what config changed in my org recently".

questions.text: Dreamhouse Realty just announced its new home concierge offering. This product is unlike anything the company has offered in the past and follows a different business model. What should the administrator configure to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A Sales Process is the stage list backing an Opportunity record type. When a new business model has stages unlike anything you've offered, the cleanest move is to create a fresh Sales Process for it (and pair with a new record type and page layout).

Quick actions are buttons, not stage lists. Approval processes don't model stages. Opportunity products are pricing line items. New Sales Process is the right fit for "different business model, different stages".

questions.text: The administrator at Ursa Major Solar has been asked to change the work Item and Project Custom Object Relationship from a master detail to a Lookup. Which scenario could prevent the administrator from fulfilling this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Roll-up summary fields are unique to master-detail relationships. If the master object has any roll-up summary fields based on the detail, you cannot convert the master-detail to a lookup — Salesforce blocks the conversion until those fields are removed.

Junction objects, lookup field values, and required-for-save constraints don't block the conversion. The roll-up summary fields on the master object are the conversion blocker.

choices.label: A
choices.text: A junction object is required to support the lookup.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The lookup field in all the records contains a value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Look-Up field is required for Saving Records.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Roll-Up summary fields exist on the master object.

questions.text: Users at Dreamhouse Realty are only allowed to see opportunities they own. Leadership wants an enterprise-wide dashboard of all open opportunities in the pipeline so that users can see how the company is performing at any point in time. How should an administrator create the dashboard without changing any sharing setting?
questions.explanation:
A dashboard's "running user" determines whose security context drives the data. To show enterprise-wide pipeline regardless of who views, set the running user to a high-privilege user (e.g. someone with View All on Opportunity). The viewers' own private model still applies elsewhere — it's just this dashboard that sees everything.

Folder permissions and filter-by-owner-role don't expose records the viewer can't normally see. Per-profile dashboards multiply maintenance. The running-user override is the precise feature.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Update the dashboard folder settings to manager for the sales reps role.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add a filter to the dashboard to filter the opportunities by owner role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Build individual dashboards for profiles that need to see the enterprise results.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a dashboard with the running User set as someone who can see all Opportunities

questions.text: An administrator at Dreamhouse Realty needs to create customized pages for the Salesforce mobile app. Which two types of pages could an administrator build and customize using the Lightning App Builder? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Lightning App Builder lets you build two main types of pages relevant to mobile: App Pages (an app-level page accessible from a navigation tab/menu — e.g. a custom home for your app), and Record Pages (the page shown when a user opens a record). Both render in the Salesforce mobile app.

User Page and Dashboard Page aren't standard Lightning App Builder page types. App Page + Record Page is the correct pair.

questions.text: An administrator at Cloud Kicks wants to deactivate a user who has left the company. What are two reasons that would prevent a user from being deactivated? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two specific situations block deactivation: the user is part of a Territory hierarchy (must be removed from territories first), or the user is referenced as a recipient of a workflow Email Alert (must be removed from those recipients first). Salesforce surfaces specific error messages for each.

Custom hierarchy field references and being highest in the role hierarchy can be inconvenient but don't actually block deactivation. Territory and email-alert references are the two hard blockers.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The user is part of a territory hierarchy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The User is in a Custom hierarchy field.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The User is assigned in workflow email alert.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The User is the highest role in the role hierarchy

questions.text: An administrator has been asked to change the data type of an auto number to text field. What should the administrator be aware of before changing the field?
questions.explanation:
Auto-Number is a special field type that generates a sequence value on insert. Salesforce explicitly prevents converting Auto-Number to Text because the conversion would require deciding what to do with existing values, and the platform doesn't support a clean migration path.

Existing values aren't preserved/converted/deleted because the conversion isn't allowed at all. The correct statement is that the conversion is prevented.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Existing field values will remain unchanged.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Existing field values will be Converted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Existing field values will be deleted.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Existing auto number field to Text is prevented.

questions.text: Sales Users at Cloud Kicks are requesting that the data in the industry field on the Account object displays on the Opportunity page layout. Which type of field should an administrator create to accomplish this?
questions.explanation:
A Cross-Object Formula Field walks a relationship to read fields on a related record. On Opportunity, a formula like Account.Industry pulls the Account's Industry value through the lookup and shows it on the Opportunity page layout — no manual copy required.

Custom or standard Account fields live on Account, not Opportunity. A new master-detail isn't needed. Cross-object formula is the lightweight, declarative way.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants to have consistency when communicating with customers on cases. The company has requested messages to be sent in an email channel with categories to help search for the proper message. Which solution should the administrator suggest to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Email Templates with shared, reusable content provide consistency. Salesforce includes prebuilt templates for common case communications, and admins can extend with custom ones organized by folder or category. Agents pick the right template, the body is consistent, and customers receive professional, predictable replies.

Quick Texts are short snippets (signatures, greetings) inserted into ad-hoc messages. Flow Templates and Auto-Responses serve different needs. Prebuilt Email Templates are the right primitive for "consistent emails I can search for".

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks updated the custom object Event to include a lookup field to the primary contact for the event. When running an event report, they want to reference fields from the associated contact record. What should the administrator do to pull contact fields into the custom report?
questions.explanation:
Custom Report Types define which fields are reportable. When you add a lookup-related object to a custom report type, the related object's fields become available in the field picker. Edit the existing Event report type's layout in Setup > Report Types and add the Contact fields you want exposed.

A new report type is overkill if the existing one can be extended. Cross-object formula fields require maintenance. Editing the existing CRT is the cleanest approach.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure formula fields on event to populate contact information

choices.label: B
choices.text: Edit the custom Event report type and add fields related via lookup.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a new report type with event as the primary object and Contact as a related object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use a dashboard with filters to show Event and Contact data as requested.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants to track shoe designs by products. Shoe designs should be unable to be deleted, and there can be multiple designs for one product across various stages. Which two steps should the administrator configure to meet this requirement? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two minimal steps create a "shoe designs hang off Products, can't be orphaned" model: create a Custom Object for shoe design (so it has its own table and lifecycle), and add a Master-Detail relationship from Shoe Design to Product (which makes Product the owner; deleting Product cascades; orphans are impossible).

A lookup wouldn't prevent orphans. The standard "design" object isn't a thing. Custom object + master-detail is the right pair.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a Custom Object for shoe design.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure a Custom Lookup Field for shoe design on the product object.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a custom master detail field for shoe design on the Product Object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the Standard Object for designs.

questions.text: The VP of Sales at Cloud Kicks is receiving an error message that prevents them from saving an Opportunity. The administrator attempted the same edit without receiving an error. How can the administrator validate the error the user is receiving?
questions.explanation:
The "Login as" feature lets a System Administrator impersonate another user and reproduce exactly what that user sees and does, including which validation/sharing/permission errors fire. That's the fastest way to validate a user-reported error you can't reproduce as yourself.

Editing the page layout, viewing audit trails, and reviewing sharing all help diagnose, but Login As actually reproduces the user's session and is usually the quickest first step.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has the organization wide defaults for Opportunity set to private. Which two features should the administrator use to open up access to Opportunity records for sales users working on collaborative deals? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
With private OWDs, two complementary mechanisms open access. Role Hierarchy gives users above an owner inherited access to that owner's records. Sharing Rules (criteria-based or owner-based) extend access to public groups, roles, or territories beyond hierarchy.

A "Sharing Set" applies to Experience Cloud users, not internal sales reps. Profiles control object-level CRUD, not record visibility. Role Hierarchy + Sharing Rules are the canonical pair for opening up record access.

questions.text: The administrator at AW Computing wants Account Details, related list and chatter feeds to each appear on separate tabs when reviewing an account. Which type of page should the administrator create?
questions.explanation:
Lightning Record Pages can host Tabs components that organize content into separate tabs. By creating a record page in Lightning App Builder and using Tabs, "Details", "Related", and "Chatter" each get their own tab — a clean, common record-page pattern.

Lightning App Pages are app-level, not per-record. "Lightning page Tab" and "Lightning page Component" aren't real types. Lightning Record Page (with the Tabs component) is the answer.

questions.text: When a Cloud Kicks Opportunity closes, the company would like to automatically create a renewal opportunity. Which two automation tools should an administrator use to accomplish this request? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two complementary tools handle "when an opportunity closes, create a renewal opportunity": Process Builder triggers on the close-won transition, and Flow Builder defines the actual logic of populating the new opportunity (Close Date next year, copying line items, etc.). Process Builder calls the autolaunched flow.

Approval Process and Workflow Rule don't create related records as cleanly. Process Builder + Flow is the standard combination for "react to a record event by creating a new related record".

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants to give credit to Opportunity team members based on the level of effort contributed by each person toward each deal. What feature should the administrator use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Opportunity Splits assign credit on a deal across multiple users — overlay splits or revenue splits — based on the level of contribution. Reports then attribute the right share to each contributor.

Stages mark the deal's progression. Queues are work containers. List Views display records. Splits is the precise feature for "give credit to each contributor in proportion to their effort".

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters has a new flow that automatically sets the field values when a new account is created. The flow is launched by a process, but the flow is not working properly. What should the administrator do to identify the problem?
questions.explanation:
Flow Builder's Debug runs the flow with inputs you specify and shows the path it took, the values at each variable, and any errors. For a flow that's not creating records as expected, Debug surfaces exactly where logic diverges or where a Create Records element fails.

Login-level debug logs are for Apex/triggers. Setup Audit Trail tracks setup changes. Email logs track emails. Flow's native Debug is the targeted tool.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the native debug feature in the flow builder.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Review debug logs with the login level.

choices.label: C
choices.text: View the setup audit Trail and review for errors.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set up Email logs and review the send error log.

questions.text: The sales manager at Cloud Kicks approves time off for their employees. They asked the administrator to ensure these requests are seen and responded to by a backup manager while the sales manager is out on vacation. What should an administrator use to fulfill the requirement?
questions.explanation:
Delegated Approver lets a user designate another user to approve on their behalf when they're out. Approval requests still arrive but the delegate can also act, so the queue doesn't pile up while the primary approver is on vacation.

Two-step approval changes the policy itself. Approval History Related List shows past approvals. Delegated Administrator delegates user/permission management, not approvals. Delegated Approver is the precise feature.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar offers amazing experiences for all of its employees. The Employee engagement committee wants to post updates while restricting other employees from posting. What should the administrator create to meet this request?
questions.explanation:
A Chatter Broadcast Group is a group where only owners and managers can post, but anyone can comment. That is exactly the "committee posts updates; others can react but not initiate" pattern.

Chatter Streams aggregate feeds. Recommendations suggest groups. Unlisted Groups hide membership but don't restrict posting. Broadcast Group is the right type.

questions.text: A sales rep at Ursa Major Solar has launched a series of networking events. They are hosting one event per month and want to be able to report on campaign ROI by month and series. How should the administrator set up the Campaign to simplify reporting?
questions.explanation:
Campaign Hierarchy lets you nest campaigns under a parent campaign. The parent rolls up child statistics (responses, won opportunities, ROI) so you can report at both the series level and the individual event level — exactly what you need for "monthly events under a series".

Record types organize layouts but don't aggregate. Same-named individual campaigns are confusing and don't roll up. Campaign Member Statuses track attendance, not series ROI. Campaign Hierarchy is built for this.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add different record types for the monthly event types.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create individual Campaigns that all have the same name.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Configure campaign Member Statuses to record which event members attended.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use Campaign Hierarchy where the monthly events roll up to a parent Campaign

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has a custom object called Shipments. The Company wants to see all the shipment items from an Account page. When an Account is deleted, the shipments should remain. What type of relationship should the administrator make between Shipments and Account?
questions.explanation:
A Lookup relationship between Shipments and Account creates a one-to-many link without ownership cascade. Shipments display on the Account page, but deleting the Account doesn't delete its shipments — they survive as orphans, which is what's required.

Master-detail would cascade-delete shipments when an Account goes. The lookup direction must be Shipments→Account so each shipment points to its account. Shipments-with-lookup-to-Account is the correct shape.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Shipments should have a lookup to Account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Accounts should have a lookup to Shipments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Shipments should have a master-detail to Accounts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Accounts should have a master-detail to Shipments.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters uses a custom object Invoice to collect customer payment information from an external billing system. The Billing System field needs to be filled on every Invoice record. How should an administrator ensure this requirement?
questions.explanation:
The "Required" checkbox on a custom field makes it universally required at save time across the UI, API, web-to-X, and other entry paths. For "this must be filled on every record", that's the right setting.

Process Builder can't enforce required fields. Approval processes don't require fields. Record-type-level required isn't a thing — you'd require at the field or layout level. Universal required at the field is the cleanest.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a Process Builder to set the field.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Define an approval process for the child.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Require the field on the record type.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has a team of product owners that need a space to share feedback and ideas with just the product team. How should the administrator leverage Salesforce to help the team collaborate?
questions.explanation:
A Chatter Private Group is invite-only — only members can see the group's posts and members. That gives the product team a private channel to share feedback and ideas without external visibility.

Quick Actions log communication on records, not group conversations. Chatter Public Group is visible to everyone. Activity History is for tasks/events. Chatter Private Group is the right type.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use Quick Actions to log communication.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add Activity History to document tasks.

questions.text: An analytics user at Cloud Kicks needs Read, Create, and Edit access for objects and should be restricted from deleting any records. What should the administrator do to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A custom Profile is the cleanest way to grant Read/Create/Edit but withhold Delete on each object. Permission sets are additive — they grant but don't revoke — so you can't use them to remove Delete that the base profile gives. Cloning a base profile and unchecking Delete per object is the standard build.

System Admin gives too much. View All + role hierarchy doesn't restrict deletes. Permission set with C/E/R doesn't remove Delete from the base. Custom Profile is the right answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assign the standard System Administrator profile to the analytical user.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Give the user View all access and assign them to the highest role in the role hierarchy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create and assign a custom profile with Delete access removed for each object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create and assign a permission set that includes Read, Create, and Edit access

questions.text: Universal Containers has enabled Data Protection and Privacy for its org. Which page layouts will have the Individual field available for tracking data privacy information?
questions.explanation:
When Data Protection and Privacy is enabled, the Individual object exists to capture privacy preferences, and an Individual lookup field becomes available on Contact, Lead, and Person Account — the three "person" objects whose privacy settings matter.

Case, Opportunity, Account (business), User, etc. don't get the Individual field. Contact + Lead + Person Account is the canonical trio.

questions.text: The administrator for Cloud Kicks needs to give access to a new custom object with custom fields to more than one user. Which two options should an administrator use to meet this requirement? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two combinations grant access to a custom object with custom fields for multiple users: create a Permission Set that grants object + field access (single source of truth), and assign a Permission Set Group containing it to multiple users at once (efficient for groups). Together they let you grant the access once and apply it broadly.

Manual sharing is per-record, not per-object grant. OWDs don't grant CRUD. Permission Set + Permission Set Group is the correct pair.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assign permission set group to Users

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants to update a screen flow so that if the checkbox field High Value Customer is set to true, the first screen is skipped and the user is directed to the second screen. How should the administrator configure the decision element?
questions.explanation:
A Decision element with the path "if High Value Customer = true, skip" needs to compare against the boolean global True constant: {!$GlobalConstant.True}. Using equals + that constant is precise and reads naturally in the flow.

Comparing to the literal string "High Value Customer" doesn't make sense for a boolean field. Contains is for text/multi-select. The equals + GlobalConstant.True is the right combination.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the equals operator and {!$GlobalConstant.True} as the value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use the equals operator and 'High Value Customer' as the value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use the contains operator and {!$GlobalConstant.False} as the value.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the contains operator and 'High Value Customer' as the value

questions.text: The administrator at Ursa Major Solar imported records into an object by mistake. Which two tools should be used to undo this import? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
If you imported the wrong records, two tools can clean up. Mass Delete Records (Setup > Data Management) deletes records matching criteria up to a limit. Data Loader can bulk-delete using a CSV of IDs you exported from the bad import — efficient for thousands of rows.

Weekly Data Export is one-way out. Data Import Wizard imports, doesn't delete. Mass Delete + Data Loader is the cleanup pair.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar wants to assist users with a guided expense report process to simplify submissions, routing, and authorizations. Which two tools should an administrator use to build this solution? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Approval Process drives the multi-step routing (submitter → manager → director). Flow Builder builds the friendly user-facing wizard for entering the expense data. Together they form a guided submission and approval experience.

Validation Rule blocks saves but isn't a wizard. Quick Action launches a flow but isn't itself the routing. Flow + Approval Process is the right combination.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters has asked an administrator to ensure that when a contact with a title of CEO is created, the contact's account record gets updated with the CEO's name. Which feature should an administrator use to implement this request?
questions.explanation:
Process Builder fires on Contact insert/update with a criterion of Title = 'CEO'. The action then updates the related Account's CEO field with the contact's name. Process Builder excels at "when child changes, update parent" with no code.

Quick Actions don't auto-fire. Workflow Rules can update fields but cross-object updates are limited (only via master-detail). Validation Rules block saves. Process Builder is the right tool.

questions.text: New leads need to be routed to the correct Sales person based on the lead address. What should an administrator use?
questions.explanation:
Lead Assignment Rules route incoming leads to users or queues based on criteria — including geographic fields like Country, State, or postal code. The rule fires on lead create (or via an explicit reassign) and assigns the right rep automatically.

Validation rules and formula fields don't assign owners. Escalation rules apply to cases, not leads. Lead Assignment Rule is the precise mechanism for territory-based lead routing.

questions.text: Users at Universal Containers would like to visually see the sales stages on an Opportunity page. The administrator is configuring path for Opportunities. Which is an important consideration for path configuration?
questions.explanation:
Path provides an inline stage tracker plus a Key Fields panel and Guidance for Success — short tips and reminders relevant to each stage. Configure both per stage and reps see exactly what to focus on right now.

Kanban is a separate view, not part of Path. The Owner field isn't typically edited in Path. Celebrations CAN be added to Path (a confetti animation on win). The most accurate consideration is that Path can include guidance and key fields per stage.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Kanban views for Path must be configured manually.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Owner field can be edited in the key fields Panel.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Celebrations are unable to be added to a path.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Path can include guidance and key fields for each stage.

questions.text: Which tool should an administrator use to identify and fix potential session vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation:
Security Health Check (Setup > Health Check) compares your security settings against a Salesforce-recommended baseline (or a custom one) and produces a score plus a list of items below baseline. It's the quickest way to surface session-related and other security gaps and prioritize fixes.

Field History Tracking and Setup Audit Trail show changes, not vulnerabilities. OWDs are one of many controls Health Check evaluates. Health Check is the dedicated tool for this.

questions.text: Which three items are available in the mobile navigation menu? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
The Salesforce mobile navigation menu can include a curated set of items: Lightning App Pages (custom mobile-friendly pages built in Lightning App Builder), Chatter (the social feed), and Dashboards (mobile-rendered dashboards). All three are pickable when you build the mobile nav.

Lightning Home Page is desktop. Utility Bar is desktop-Lightning, not mobile. App Pages + Chatter + Dashboards is the canonical mobile-nav set.

questions.text: Support agents at Cloud Kicks are spending too much time finding resources to solve cases. The agents need a more efficient way to find documentation and similar cases from the Case page layout. How should an administrator meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Salesforce Knowledge with data-categorized articles is the right primitive. Articles surface inline (via the Knowledge component or related list) on the Case page, filtered by data categories that match the case — agents see relevant solutions without searching.

Custom objects + flows + global search all add work without delivering Knowledge's article framework. Knowledge with data categories is the targeted answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a custom object to capture popular case resolutions.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use an interview flow to capture Case details.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Direct users to Global Search to look for similar cases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure Knowledge with articles and data categories.

questions.text: DreamHouse Realty needs to use consistent picklist values in the category field on accounts and cases, with values respective to record types. (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two complementary picklist mechanics solve "consistent values per record type": Dependent Picklists (one picklist filters another based on the controlling value, e.g. Account Type filters Category), and Global Picklists (a value set shared across multiple objects/fields so Account.Category and Case.Category use the same master list).

Multi-select is a UX format. Custom picklist alone doesn't enforce consistency across objects. Dependent + Global Picklists is the right pair.

questions.text: Universal Containers (UC) customers have provided feedback that their support cases are not being responded to quickly enough. UC wants to send all unassigned Cases that have been open for more than two hours to an urgent Case queue and alert the support manager. Which feature should an administrator configure to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Case Escalation Rules with a 2-hour aging trigger move stale unassigned cases to an urgent queue and fire an email alert to the support manager. One mechanism, both outcomes.

Scheduled Reports and Dashboard Refreshes don't act on individual cases. Assignment Rules fire on create. Escalation Rule is the precise time-based response feature.

questions.text: An administrator at Universal Containers needs an automated way to delete records based on field values. What automated solution should the administrator use?
questions.explanation:
Flow Builder is the modern, recommended automation. With Get Records and Delete Records elements (and a scheduled or invocable trigger), you can find records matching field criteria and delete them programmatically without code.

Workflow Rule and Process Builder cannot delete records. Automation Studio is a Marketing Cloud tool. Flow Builder is the only Salesforce platform tool that can delete in bulk declaratively.

questions.text: The Human Resources department at Northern Trail Outfitters wants employees to provide feedback about their manager using a custom object in Salesforce. It is important that managers are unable to see the feedback records from their staff. How should an administrator configure the custom object to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
For OWDs to apply tightly enough that managers can't see their team's feedback, uncheck "Grant Access Using Hierarchies" on the custom object. That disables the implicit hierarchy-based access for that object alone, so private OWDs really mean private — even from the role hierarchy.

Sharing rules grant, not restrict. External access affects portal users. Owner-based sharing rules grant access. Unchecking "Grant Access Using Hierarchies" is the unique knob that closes the hierarchy back-channel.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set the default external access to private.

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks has been asked to change the company's Shoe Style field to prevent users from selecting more than one style on a record. Which two steps should an administrator do to accomplish this? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two steps eliminate multi-select on the field. First, change the field type from Multi-Select Picklist to Picklist (the regular single-value flavor) — that constrains storage to a single chosen value. Second, the regular picklist UI does not allow multiple selections, satisfying the "only one style at a time" requirement.

Reactivating values isn't necessary. Backing up values is good hygiene but not the operative step. Type change to single-value Picklist is what actually enforces the constraint. (The "Choose only one value" wording in the question maps to the regular Picklist behavior.)

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reactivate the appropriate Shoe Style values after the field type changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Select the 'Choose only one value' checkbox on the picklist field.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Back-up the Shoe Style values in existing records.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the field type from a multi-select picklist field to a picklist field.

questions.text: Universal Containers administrator has been asked to create a many-to-many relationship between two existing custom objects. Which two steps should the administrator take when enabling the many-to-many relationship? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
A many-to-many model in Salesforce is built with a junction object — a custom object that has master-detail relationships to both other objects. Each junction record represents one pairing, and the two MDs together give you the many-to-many cardinality plus shared sharing/ownership.

A single lookup gives only one-to-many. URL fields are unrelated. Junction object + two master-detail relationships is the canonical many-to-many pattern.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a junction with a custom object.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create two master detail relationships on the new object.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create two lookup relationships on the new object.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create URL fields on a custom object.

questions.text: A user at Universal Containers left the company. The administrator needs to create a new user for their replacement, but they have assigned all available user licenses. What should the administrator do to free up user licenses for the new users?
questions.explanation:
Deactivating a user releases the user license back to the pool while preserving all their historical data, ownership, audit logs, and references. The new hire then claims the freed license.

Deleting users isn't supported (you'd lose history). Freezing only blocks login; the license stays consumed. Repointing the old record to the new hire is brittle and undermines audit. Deactivate is the standard play.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deactivate the former employee's user record.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Change the former user's record to the new user.

questions.text: The events manager at DreamHouse Realty has a hot lead from a successful open house that needs to become a contact with an associated opportunity. How should this be accomplished from the campaign keeping the associated campaign member history?
questions.explanation:
When you convert a lead from inside a Campaign Member detail page, the resulting Contact (and Opportunity) preserve the linkage to that campaign — the campaign member history follows the conversion automatically. That's the cleanest way to keep the marketing-source attribution intact.

Deleting and recreating loses history. Cloning then converting won't preserve the original lead's campaign association. Adding a contact creates a new record without the lead's context. Convert from the campaign member detail page is the right path.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delete the lead and create a new contact and opportunity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clone the lead and convert the cloned record to a contact.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Convert the lead from the campaign member detail page.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add a contact from a campaign member detail page.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has the organization-wide sharing default set to private on the Shoe object. The sales manager should be able to view a report containing shoe records for all of the sales reps on their team. Which 3 items should the administrator configure to provide appropriate access to the report? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
Three pieces line up so the sales manager can run that report. A Custom Report Type that includes Shoe and the manager's reportable fields. Folder access on the report folder so the manager can see and run the report. Field-Level Security so the columns the report shows aren't masked for the manager's profile.

A subscription mails a copy on a schedule but doesn't grant access. CRT + Folder + FLS is the right trio for "team report against private data".

questions.text: The sales team at Ursa Major Solar has asked the administrator to automate an outbound message. What should the administrator utilize to satisfy the request?
questions.explanation:
Workflow Rule still ships an Outbound Message action that POSTs SOAP to a configured endpoint. For a no-code "send this to an external system on save" need, the Workflow Rule + Outbound Message pairing is the historical and still-valid pattern.

Process Builder doesn't have a native outbound message action (you'd call a Flow). Flow itself doesn't have a built-in SOAP message; it does HTTP callouts via Apex. Task assignment is unrelated. Workflow Rule with outbound message is the precise tool.

questions.text: Sales managers would like to know what could be implemented to surface important values based on the stage of the opportunity. Which tool should an administrator use to meet the requirement?
questions.explanation:
Path's Key Fields panel surfaces stage-relevant fields directly on the record page as a rep advances stages. Salespeople see (and can edit inline) exactly the fields that matter at the current stage — no scrolling through a long layout.

Dynamic Forms are about per-field visibility on the record body. Opportunity processes (sales processes) define stages, not field surfacing. Workflow rules don't surface fields. Path Key Fields is the right tool.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks needs to ensure appropriate shipping details are used in orders. Reps should have a streamlined solution to update the shipping address on selected orders associated with an account when the shipping address is changed on the account. How should the administrator deliver this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A Screen Flow on the Account page lets the rep choose which open associated orders should adopt the new shipping address. That control matters: not every order should auto-update (some may already be shipping). The flow gathers selections and updates only the chosen orders.

An autolaunched flow on either object is automatic with no choice. A screen flow on the Order page would mean editing one at a time. Screen flow on the Account page is the precise UX.

choices.label: A

questions.text: The administrator at Universal Containers has a screen flow that helps users create new leads. When lead source is 'Search Engine', the administrator needs to require the user to choose a specific search engine from a picklist. If lead source is not 'Search Engine', this picklist should be hidden. How should the administrator complete this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Conditional Visibility on a screen-component lets you show or hide a field based on the value of another field on the same screen. Setting the search-engine picklist's visibility to "show when LeadSource = 'Search Engine'" is a one-click pattern, no extra screens or assignments.

A new screen disrupts flow. An assignment doesn't hide UI. A validation rule doesn't hide fields. Conditional visibility is the precise feature.

choices.label: B

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure a picklist for specific search engine, and use a validation rule to conditionally show only when lead source is 'Search Engine'

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks is trying to debug a screen flow that creates contacts. One of the variables in the flow is missing on the debug screen. What could cause this issue?
questions.explanation:
In Flow Debug, only variables marked "Available for input" show up as inputs you can supply on the debug screen. If a variable isn't appearing for input there, the most common cause is that checkbox is unchecked.

Inactive flow versions still debug. Field types are debuggable across the standard set. The "Available for output" flag controls whether the variable is exposed when the flow is called from elsewhere — not the debug-input panel. The input-availability flag is the right thing to verify.

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

questions.text: Cloud Kicks executives have noticed the opportunity Expected Revenue field displays incorrect values. How should the administrator correct this?
questions.explanation:
Expected Revenue is computed as Amount × Probability. If the displayed Expected Revenue looks wrong, the operative input is the Probability tied to each Stage (since Stage drives Probability by default). Adjust the Probability values per stage and Expected Revenue normalizes.

The Expected Revenue field doesn't have a per-stage override of its own. Forecast category and Closed Won values affect different things. Probability tied to stages is what corrects the calculation.

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

choices.text: Change the probability associated with the stage.

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks has been told that users are unable to add repeating tasks in Salesforce. Which two solutions should the administrator use to ensure users are able to do this? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two configuration steps make recurring tasks available. Enable "Recurring Tasks" in Activity Settings, and add the "Create Recurring Series of Tasks" field/region to the Task page layouts so users can actually configure recurrence when creating a task.

Disabling Shared Activities is unrelated. Task Notifications service is for digest emails. Activity Settings toggle + page layout exposure is the right pair.

questions.text: An administrator at Northern Trail Outfitters is unable to add a new user in Salesforce. What could cause this issue?
questions.explanation:
Salesforce usernames must be unique across all Salesforce orgs in the world (they look like email addresses but they're actually globally unique IDs). If someone has used the desired username — even in a different org — you can't reuse it. Append a suffix to make it unique.

Corporate-email constraints, length checks, and "fake email" aren't enforced rules. Already-in-use is the genuine block.

questions.text: The DreamHouse Realty team has a master-detail relationship set up with open house as the parent object and visitors as the child object. What type of field should the administrator add to the open house object to track number of visitors?
questions.explanation:
A Roll-Up Summary field on the master object (Open House) can COUNT the children (Visitors). It's the right field type for "count related child records" in a master-detail relationship.

Multi-select picklist stores fixed picklist values. Cross-object formula reads a single field, not aggregates. Indirect lookup is for cross-org references. Roll-Up Summary is the canonical choice for child counts.

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks deleted a custom field but realized there is a business unit that still uses the field. What should an administrator take into consideration when undeleting the field?
questions.explanation:
Salesforce holds a deleted custom field (and its data) for ~15 days, but field history data is permanently lost when you delete the field. Even if you undelete the field within the window, the history of value changes that field had cannot be recovered.

Reports and page layouts often need re-adding, but the irrecoverable item is the field history. The recycle bin holds records, not fields. Field history loss is the gotcha to watch.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The field needs to be re-added to reports.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The field history will remain deleted.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The field needs to be restored from the recycle bin.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The field needs to be re-added to page Layouts.

questions.text: An administrator needs to create a one-to-many relationship between two objects with limited access to child records. What type of field should the administrator use?
questions.explanation:
A Lookup field creates a one-to-many relationship and lets you control access independently. Profile field permissions can hide it; sharing on the lookup target object is independent of the lookup parent. That gives you "limited access to child records" — a master-detail would force the child's access to follow the parent.

Roll-up summary is a field type, not a relationship. Cross-object formula reads, doesn't link. Master-detail forces shared access. Lookup is the right one-to-many with independent access.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to use contact hierarchy in its org to display contact association. What should the administrator take into consideration regarding the contact hierarchy?
questions.explanation:
The Contact Hierarchy view honors record-level access — users only see contacts they're allowed to see. The hierarchy doesn't bypass sharing; it respects it.

Hierarchy size limits are higher than 3,000. Customizing hierarchy columns affects only the hierarchy itself, not list views. Sharing is honored, not ignored. Record-level access driving visibility is the correct consideration.

questions.text: The administrator at Ursa Major Solar has created a custom report type and built a report for the sales operation team. However, none of the users are able to access the report. Which two options could cause this issue? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two issues make a custom-report-type-based report invisible to others. First, the CRT itself can be in "In Development" mode, which keeps it hidden from non-admins. Second, the report can be saved in a private folder where only the owner sees it.

Profile View access on standard reports is one factor but doesn't apply to admin-built CRTs the same way. CRT limits are very high. Development status + private folder are the two common causes.

questions.text: Sales reps at Ursa Major Solar are having difficulty managing deals. The leadership team has asked the administrator to help sales reps prioritize and close more deals. What should the administrator configure?
questions.explanation:
Einstein Opportunity Scoring scores each opportunity 1–99 based on patterns from your historical wins/losses. Reps see the score on the opportunity and on list views, so they can prioritize the most-likely-to-close deals.

Activity Capture syncs email/calendar. Search Personalization tunes search results. Lead Scoring is for leads, not opportunities. Opportunity Scoring is the precise feature for closing more deals.

questions.text: The administrator for AW Computing is working with a user who is having trouble logging in to Salesforce. What should the administrator do to identify why the user is unable to login?
questions.explanation:
The Login History (Setup > Login History) shows recent login attempts: timestamp, status (success/failure), IP, browser, login type, and reason for failure. That's the first place to look for "why can't this user log in?"

Security tokens, password history, and password policies all matter, but Login History tells you concretely whether the user even reached the login page successfully and why it failed.

questions.text: Once an opportunity reaches the negotiation stage at Cloud Kicks, the Amount field becomes required for sales users. Sales managers need to be able to move opportunities into this stage without knowing the amount. How should the administrator require this field during the negotiation stage for sales users but allow their managers to make changes?
questions.explanation:
A Validation Rule with a profile-aware exemption is the precise mechanism. The formula checks: when StageName = 'Negotiation' AND Amount is blank AND the user's profile is NOT 'Sales Manager', block. Sales managers are exempted; reps are required.

Universally required is too broad. A formula field for managers doesn't gate save. Switching managers to admin profile breaks other security. Validation rule with profile check is the targeted answer.

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters has hired interns to enter Leads into Salesforce and has requested a way to identify these new records from existing Leads. What approach should an administrator take to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A Record Type for "Intern Lead" lets you tag those leads distinctly while keeping a shared layout. Reports and list views can filter on record type to identify the intern-sourced leads at a glance.

Web-to-Lead requires a public form (different scenario). A separate Lightning App is heavy. Lead Assignment Rule changes does not segment new from existing. Record Type is the lightweight, native answer.

questions.text: The Cloud Kicks sales manager wants to boost productivity by providing insights at the start of each day. Which three sales-specific standard Lightning components should administrator add to the homepage to meet this requirement? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
Three sales-specific Lightning components on the Home page give reps daily focus. Activities (today's tasks/events tied to records). Assistant (a curated list of items needing attention — overdue tasks, leads requiring follow-up). Key Deals (top opportunities for the day). Together they make the home page actionable.

Path is per-record, not home. Performance Chart is also useful but the trio of Activities + Assistant + Key Deals is the canonical set for "boost productivity at the start of each day".

questions.text: What are three settings an administrator should configure to make it easy for approvers to respond to approval requests? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
Three settings make approvers' lives easier. Enable Chatter approvals (so requests can be approved from the feed). Enable email approval responses (reply with APPROVE/REJECT in plain email). Add the "Items to Approve" component to approvers' Home pages so they see pending items immediately.

Specifying initial submission actions doesn't make the approval easier — it's about side-effects of submission. Auto-approve flows defeat the purpose of an approval. Chatter + email + Items-to-Approve component is the right trio.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Update the organization's chatter setting to allow approvals.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable the organization's Email approval response setting.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Specify initial submission actions within the approval process.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add the Items to approve component to the approvers home page.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Create a flow to automatically approve all records.

questions.text: New Leads need to be routed to the correct sales person based on the lead address. How should the administrator configure this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Lead Assignment Rules route based on field values, including geographic fields. Configure rules with criteria on State/Country/postal code and the matching rule entry assigns to the corresponding sales person. The rule fires on lead create or via reassign.

Formula fields and validation rules don't assign owners. Escalation rules are for cases. Lead Assignment Rule is the right routing tool.

questions.text: An administrator at DreamHouse Realty wants an easier way to assign an agent capacity and skill set. Which feature should the administrator enable to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Omni-Channel routes work to agents based on per-agent capacity and skill set. With Omni-Channel and Skills configured, the platform automatically pushes the right item to an available agent — no manual assignment.

Knowledge Management organizes articles. Escalation Rules act on aging cases. Territory Management is about account assignment. Omni-Channel is the precise feature for capacity + skill routing.

questions.text: Universal Containers has a contact Lightning record page with a component that shows LinkedIn data. The sales team would like to only show this component to sales users when they are on their mobile phones. (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two filters make a component show only to mobile sales users. Filter by User Profile name = 'Sales User' (or whatever profile is correct), and filter by Form Factor = Phone (so it doesn't show on desktop). Both must be satisfied — Lightning App Builder ANDs filters by default.

Form Factor isn't "Mobile/Tablet" — it's the discrete value Phone, Tablet, or Desktop. Role isn't typically used to gate UI. Profile + Form Factor = Phone is the right combination.

questions.text: At Cloud Kicks sales reps use discounts on the opportunity record to help win sales on products. When an opportunity is won, they then have to manually apply the discount to the related opportunity products. The sales manager has asked if there is a way to automate this time-consuming task. What should the administrator use to deliver this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Flow Builder can trigger on opportunity update (record-triggered, after-save) and use a Get Records to fetch related Opportunity Products, then Update Records with the discount applied. All declarative, no code.

Approval Process drives review. Macros operate on lists from a console. Formula fields don't write back. Flow Builder is the right automation for "on close-won, update related records".

questions.text: DreamHouse Realty agents are double-booking open house event nights. The event manager wants the event submission process to help agents fill in event details and request dates. How should an administrator accomplish the request?
questions.explanation:
An Approval Process on the Campaign object models the request: agents submit a campaign (event) for approval, the event manager (or homeowners' association in the question's framing) reviews and approves, and the calendar conflict can be screened during approval.

Workflow Rule for date update doesn't model approval. Sharing rule changes visibility, not approval. Creating a campaign is the data model — the approval process is the missing review piece. Approval Process on Campaign is the right answer.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks intends to protect data with backups by using the Data Export Service. Which two considerations should the administrator remember when scheduling the export? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two Data Export Service constraints to remember: data exports run weekly or monthly (no daily option), and the service exports only data — metadata backups (objects, fields, layouts, code) require a separate process like Metadata API, Change Sets, or Source Tracking.

Sandbox refresh intervals don't constrain data export. Data Export should run from production for real backups. Weekly/monthly cadence + metadata-needs-separate-tooling is the right pair.
