questions.text: Cloud Kicks needs to change the owner of a case when it has been open for more than 7 days. How should the administrator complete this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Case Escalation Rules with a 7-day age trigger reassign the case owner. The escalation action set explicitly includes "change case owner", which is the operative outcome here.

Auto-Response Rules send emails. Validation Rule blocks saves. Assignment Rule fires on create. Escalation Rule on age + change-owner action is the right fit.

questions.text: The administrator has been asked to automate a simple field update on the account. When a support agent changes the status of the account to 'Audited', they would like the system to automatically update the Audited date field on the account with today's date. Which tool should the administrator use to complete this automation?
questions.explanation:
A Formula Field with the formula CASE(Status, 'Audited', TODAY(), null) (or similar) auto-displays today's date when the status flips. Formula fields recompute on read, so the displayed date is always "current as of the audit".

Note: if you want to PERSIST the actual date stamped at the moment of the change (not recomputing every time), you'd use a Process Builder/Flow to write to a Date field — but the question's framing of "automatically update" with simplicity points to a formula field. (Caveat: a formula uses TODAY() so its value will reflect the current rendering date if the question semantics are about a stamp-and-store, Flow is the better answer; the answer here matches the source's intent.)

questions.text: AW Computing wants to prevent users from updating the Account Annual Revenue field to be a negative value or an amount more than $100 billion. How should an administrator accomplish this request?
questions.explanation:
A Validation Rule with formula OR(AnnualRevenue < 0, AnnualRevenue > 100000000000) blocks saves outside the allowed range. Users see a clear error and the bad value never persists.

A scheduled report finds problems after the fact. Required-on-layout doesn't constrain range. There's no setup limit toggle for arbitrary numeric ranges. Validation rule is the right enforcement.

questions.text: DreamHouse Realty (DHR) wants a templated process with a mortgage calculator that generates leads for loans. DHR needs to complete the project within 30 days and has maxed out its budget for the year. Which AppExchange item should help the administrator to meet the request?
questions.explanation:
Flow Solutions on AppExchange are pre-built flow templates you install and customize — including business-process bundles like mortgage calculators or lead generators. With a tight deadline and budget cap, picking up a Flow Solution and tweaking it is the fastest path.

Lightning Data is data enrichment. Lightning Community/Bolt Solutions are Experience Cloud templates. Flow Solutions is the precise category for installable flow logic.

questions.text: The Call centre manager in Ursa Major Solar wants to provide agents with a case dashboard that can be drilled down by case origin, status and owner. What should an administrator add to the dashboard to fulfil the request?
questions.explanation:
Dashboard Filters let viewers slice the same dashboard by field values — Origin, Status, Owner — without rebuilding. Configure up to three filters and the dashboard becomes interactively drillable.

Bucket columns categorize data. Combination chart is a chart type. Adding more components doesn't enable filtering. Dashboard Filter is the right primitive for "let agents slice this dashboard".

questions.text: Universal Containers wants to prevent its service team from accessing deal records. While service users are unable to access deal list views, they are able to find the deal records via a search. What options should the administrator adjust to fully restrict access?
questions.explanation:
If users can still find records by global search, you have to remove the underlying access at two levels: object permissions (Read/View on the profile or permission set) and tab visibility. Without object Read, search returns nothing. With tab hidden, the navigation entry is gone.

Search index isn't an admin-tunable user-facing toggle. App permissions don't control object access. Page layouts and FLS hide fields, not records. Object permissions + tab visibility is the precise restriction.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar is noticing a decrease in deals with a cross-sell opportunity type and wants to share all cross-sell opportunities with a team of subject matter experts in their organisation. The company has different roles, and the organisation wide default opportunity is set to private. How should the administrator accomplish this?
questions.explanation:
A Public Group containing the subject matter experts plus a Criteria-Based Sharing Rule keyed on Opportunity Type = 'Cross-Sell' grants the group read/edit on every cross-sell opp without changing OWDs. The rule re-evaluates as new cross-sell opps are created — automatic.

Loosening the OWD opens everything. Territory + manual sharing scales poorly. New role + owner-based sharing rule is roundabout. Public group + criteria-based sharing rule is the precise pattern.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks has a screen flow with two questions on the same screen, but only one is necessary at a time. The administrator has been asked to show only the question that is needed. How should an administrator complete this?
questions.explanation:
Conditional Visibility on a single screen lets one of the two questions stay hidden based on a flag/value. The user only sees the question that's relevant to their path — no extra screens, no branching elements.

A new flow version per scenario is overkill. A decision element + new screen disrupts UX. Branching at flow-element level isn't visibility-on-screen. Conditional Visibility is the cleanest tool.

questions.text: AW Computing would like to improve its Case Lightning record page by including: a filtered component to display a message in bold font when a case is saved as a critical record type, and a quick way to update the account status from the case layout. Which two components should an administrator use to satisfy these requests? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two Lightning components solve the request. A Related Record component embedded on the Case page exposes Account fields inline so the agent can update Account.Status without leaving the case. A Rich Text component (or component visibility on a banner) calls out the message in bold when the case record type is critical.

Related List shows multiple records. Record Details shows the case's own fields. Related Record + Rich Text covers both the inline-update and the bold-message asks.

questions.text: The administrator at Universal Containers wants to add branding to Salesforce. Which two considerations should the administrator keep in mind? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two key constraints on Salesforce themes. Only one theme can be active at any time, and it applies org-wide — you can't theme by app or by user. Also, Chatter external/community users see the built-in Lightning theme regardless of internal theming.

Themes apply to Lightning, not Salesforce Classic. Custom theme limits are higher than 150. The two correct constraints are "one theme per org" and "external Chatter users see only built-in".

questions.text: An administrator supporting a global team of Salesforce users has been asked to configure the company settings. Which two options should the administrator configure? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Default Language and Currency Locale are the two most globally-impactful Company Information settings. Default Language sets the UI labels for users without an override. Currency Locale sets the formatting and (in single-currency orgs) the org currency. Together they determine how the platform renders for everyone.

Login Hours and Password Policy are profile/security knobs, not company-wide locale. Default Language + Currency Locale is the right pair.

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks needs to automatically route support cases, regardless of how they are created, to a queue based on case priority. What tool should the administrator use?
questions.explanation:
Case Assignment Rules accept multiple criteria, including Priority. Configure rule entries that route Critical → urgent queue, High → tier-2 queue, etc. Whether the case originates from email, web, API, or manual create, the assignment rule fires.

Email-to-Case is intake, not routing logic. Auto-Response is for emails. Web-to-Case is intake. Assignment Rules are the central routing primitive that handles all origins.

questions.text: DreamHouse Realty needs to use consistent picklist values on a category field on accounts and cases, with values respective to record types. Which two features should the administrator use to fulfill this requirement? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two picklist features deliver consistency-with-record-type-aware values. Dependent Picklists tie the Category picklist's options to the controlling field (record type or another picklist). Custom Picklists let you author the value sets fresh per object so they aren't trying to reuse a one-size-fits-all global list.

Multi-select complicates value entry. Global picklist forces sharing across objects, which fights the per-record-type customization here. Dependent + Custom Picklist is the right pair for this requirement.

questions.text: At Universal Containers, there is a custom field on the Lead named Product Category. Management wants this information to be part of the Opportunity upon lead conversion. What action should the administrator take to satisfy the request?
questions.explanation:
Map the lead's custom field to a corresponding custom field on Opportunity (and/or Contact). Salesforce has a Lead Field Mapping screen specifically for this — create the destination field on Opportunity, then map Lead.Product_Category__c to it. Conversion will copy the value automatically.

Mapping to a Product field is a different object. Workflow Rules can copy fields after the fact, but the canonical solution is field mapping at conversion time. Custom field on Opportunity + map is the correct two-step.

choices.text: Create a workflow to update Opportunity fields based on the lead.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a custom field on the Opportunity and map the two fields.

choices.text: Configure the product categories picklist field on the product.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters wants to encourage employees to choose secure and appropriate passwords for their Salesforce accounts. Which three password policies should an administrator configure? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
Three of the most impactful password policies. Maximum invalid login attempts (lock account on N failures, blunting brute force). Password complexity requirements (mix of letter/number/special, raising entropy). Number of days until expiration (forces rotation).

Prohibited password values is a niche feature. Password Manager App requirement isn't a Salesforce policy. The trio above is the standard hardening set.

questions.text: An administrator at AW Computing has been asked to help the Support team with report folders. They want a folder called Support Reports and two folders underneath called Helpdesk and R&D. Support agents should be able to run Helpdesk reports, but should not be able to view R&D reports. Support managers should be able to view and edit all reports. Which two ways should these folders be shared? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two folder shares satisfy the requirements. Share the Helpdesk folder with Support Agents at View access (run reports, no edit). Share the parent Support Reports folder with Support Managers at Edit access — that grants them edit on contained subfolders too, including R&D.

Sharing R&D directly with managers and Helpdesk-with-view-only-managers achieves the same outcome but is more granular. Either approach works; the canonical answer is the parent-share for managers + child-share-view for agents.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Share the R&D folder with Support Managers with Edit Access.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Share the Helpdesk folder with Support Agents with View access.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Share the Support Reports folder with Support Managers with Edit Access.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Share the Support Reports folder with Support Agents with View Access.

questions.text: The Sales manager at DreamHouse Realty wants the sales users to have a quick way to view and edit the Opportunities in their pipeline expected to close in the next 90 days. What should an administrator do to accomplish this request?
questions.explanation:
A List View on Opportunity filtered by ExpectedCloseDate ≤ NEXT_N_DAYS:90 (and Stage open) gives a sharp list of "what's closing in the next 90 days". Switching that list to Kanban view turns it into a drag-and-drop board reps can use to update stage in place.

Custom report + scheduled email is more friction. Sales Console with per-tab opening is heavier. New dashboard with a component shows numbers, not editable records. List View + Kanban is the precise UX.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a custom report and schedule the sales users to receive it each day as a reminder to update their opportunities.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enable Sales Console and show users how to open a tab for each opportunity in the pipeline that meets the requirements.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a list view on the Opportunity object and recommend users switch the view to Kanban to edit by drag and drop.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Make a new Sales dashboard and add a component that shows all opportunities that meet the criteria.

questions.text: Which two objects are customizable in the Stage Setup Flow? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
The Stage Setup Flow is a guided UI that helps admins customize stages on Lead and Opportunity. Both objects have stage-like progressions (Lead Status, Opportunity Stage) and the wizard works for both.

Campaign and Campaign Member don't have stage flows in the same sense. Lead + Opportunity is the right pair.

questions.text: Universal Containers has three separate lines of business. Each line has specific fields that must be displayed to users. However, the fields needed by the sales team are different than the fields needed by the service team. How should the administrator configure this requirement?
questions.explanation:
With three lines of business each having different fields, and Sales vs Service teams needing different layouts, the build is three Record Types (one per line of business) and two Page Layouts per record type (one for sales, one for service) — for a total of three record types and six layouts.

Two record types or one record type doesn't capture three lines. Six record types is excessive. Three record types × two page layouts each is the right shape.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create two record types, each with 3 page layouts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create one record type with six Page Layouts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create three record types, each with 2 page layouts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create six record types, each with 1 page layout.

questions.text: Universal Containers introduced a new product and wants to track all associated cases that get logged. They are looking for an automated solution that would give the product's two lead engineers read/write access to all new cases that reference the new product. What should an administrator do to satisfy this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A Queue gathers cases the lead engineers should see, and a Criteria-Based Sharing Rule sharing case records where Product = 'New Product' to that queue (or to a public group containing the engineers) gives them read/write at the record level.

Predefined case team + assignment rule is one option but doesn't scale to "every case automatically". User-based sharing + ad-hoc team is more manual. Auto-response + public group doesn't grant access. Queue + criteria-based sharing rule is the precise build.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a queue and a criteria-based sharing rule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a predefined case team and an assignment rule.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create a user-based sharing rule and an ad-hoc case team.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create an auto-response rule and a public group.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters (NTO) has deployed My Domain. The Chief Marketing Officer wants to make sure that all of the Salesforce users log in using the branded login URL. There needs to be a grace period for the user's bookmarks to be updated. How should the administrator configure the policies in My Domain settings?
questions.explanation:
My Domain has a Redirect Policy that controls what happens when users try to reach the org via the old generic URL. "Redirect with a warning to the same page within the domain" sends them to the My Domain URL but flashes a warning so they update bookmarks gracefully — no hard cutover that breaks anyone's workflow.

"Do not redirect" leaves them on the wrong URL. "Require" forces immediate cutover with no grace. Redirect-with-warning is the gentle migration setting.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set the login policy to require login from https://nto.my.salesforce.com

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the Redirect policy to Do Not redirect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set the redirect policy to Redirect with a warning to the same page within the domain.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set the login policy to prevent login from https://login.salesforce.com

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar has service level agreements (SLA) that are routed to support queues. Cases that meet the 24 hour SLA need to be automatically re-assigned to the next tier queue. Which feature should be used to fulfill this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Case Escalation Rules can include time-based criteria (escalate after N hours that meet conditions) and reassign the case as one of the actions. Pointed at "case has been in the queue 24 hours", the rule moves the case to the next-tier queue automatically.

Einstein Case Routing uses ML for initial routing, not aging escalations. Auto-Response sends emails. Assignment Rule fires on create. Escalation Rule is the right time-based reassign tool.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks wants to track shoe designs by products. Shoe designs should be unable to be deleted, and there can be multiple designs for one product across various stages. Which two steps should the administrator configure to meet this requirement? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
A custom object for Shoe Designs paired with a custom Lookup field on the Product object lets multiple designs reference one product across various stages. The lookup direction (design → product) keeps the model flexible (you can have orphan designs if needed) while still showing all designs from the product page.

Master-detail would prevent orphans but couples lifecycle. Standard "design" object isn't a thing. Custom object + lookup is the right shape for the requirements.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a custom master-detail field for shoe designs on the Product object.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a custom object for shoe designs.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use the standard object for designs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure a custom lookup field for shoe designs on the Product object.

questions.text: Sales reps at Ursa Major Solar are having difficulty managing deals. The leadership team has asked the administrator to help sales reps prioritize and close more deals. What should the administrator configure to help with these issues?
questions.explanation:
Einstein Opportunity Scoring scores each opportunity 1–99 based on patterns in your historical wins/losses — surfaced on lists and records so reps can prioritize. That's the targeted feature for "help reps prioritize and close more deals".

Activity Capture syncs email/calendar but doesn't score. Search Personalization tunes search. Lead Scoring is for leads. Opportunity Scoring is the right tool.

questions.text: Northern Trail Outfitters has hired interns to enter Leads into Salesforce and has requested a way to identify these new records from existing Leads. What approach should an administrator take to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Define a custom Record Type for "Intern Lead" and assign it to the interns. Their leads carry that record type, distinguishing them from the existing pipeline at a glance — visible in list views, reports, and dashboards via filters on Record Type.

Web-to-Lead requires a public form (different scenario). New Lightning App is overkill. Lead Assignment Rules don't tag the records. Record Type assignment is the lightweight, native way to identify the new records.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a separate Lead Lightning App.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Define a record type and assign it to the interns.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Set up Web-to-Lead for the interns' use.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Update the active Lead Assignment Rules.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar has a path on Case. The company wants to require its users to follow the status values as they are on the path. Agents should be prohibited from reverting the Case back to a previous status. Which feature should an administrator use to fulfill this request?
questions.explanation:
A Validation Rule with PRIORVALUE() and ISCHANGED() can detect a Status going backwards on the Path and block the save. The rule's formula compares the new status's "rank" against the prior value's "rank" using a CASE() ladder.

Predefined Field Values, Global Value Picklists, and Dependent Picklists set or filter values but don't enforce a directional progression. Validation Rule is the only mechanism that can prevent backward transitions.

questions.text: An administrator at Northern Trail Outfitters is unable to add a new user in Salesforce. What could cause this issue?
questions.explanation:
Salesforce usernames are globally unique across all orgs in the world. If the candidate username has been used by anyone, anywhere, the new-user save fails. The fix is appending a suffix (.acme, .training, etc.) to make it unique.

Domain restrictions, contact-record collisions, corporate-email rules — none of these are the actual block. Already-in-use globally is the operative cause.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The username is already in use in another organization.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The username is restricted to a domain specific to my domain.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The email address used for the username has a contact record.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The email used for the username is not a corporate email address.

questions.text: An administrator at Universal Containers has been asked to prevent users from accessing Salesforce from outside of their network. What are two considerations for this configuration? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two safeguards that actually limit Salesforce access to inside the network. Set Login IP Ranges on the profile or globally so attempts from outside-allowed-IPs fail. Restrict the use of U2F Security Keys with login-hour-style policies on the user's profile to further constrain when/how they can authenticate.

SSO via permission set extends access, doesn't restrict it. Enforce-on-Every-Request is the Spring 6 toggle for API enforcement (related but a different lever). The pair flagged here is profile/global IP + U2F restrictions.

choices.label: A
choices.text: IP address restrictions are set on the profile or globally for the org.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assign single sign-on to a permission set to allow users to log in when outside the network.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enforce Login IP Ranges on Every Request must be selected to enforce IP restrictions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restrict U2F Security Keys on the user's profile to enforce login hours.

questions.text: An administrator at Northern Trail Outfitters is creating a validation rule. Which two functions should the administrator use when creating a validation rule? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
A Validation Rule definition has two essential parts. The Error Condition Formula expresses when the rule should fire (returns true to block save). The Error Message Location specifies where the error appears — at the top of the page or next to a specific field.

Formula return type is fixed at boolean for validation rules. Rule active date isn't a property. Error condition + error message location are the two operative configuration knobs.

questions.text: An administrator is planning to use Data Loader to mass import new records to a custom object from a new API. What will the administrator need to do to use the Data Loader?
questions.explanation:
When the user logs in to Data Loader from a network not in the trusted IP list, Salesforce demands the security token appended to the password (password + token concatenated). The token is reset/visible in the user's personal settings.

Permission sets and the Data Import Wizard don't apply here. Resetting password+token isn't a usage requirement; appending the token is. Append-token-to-password is the operative answer for API tools.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a permission set that allows them to import data.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Append their security token at the end of their password to login.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use the Data Import Tool to mass import custom object records.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reset their password and their security token.

questions.text: Which setting on a profile makes a tab hidden in the All App Launcher or visible in any app, but still allows a user to view records that would normally be found under this tab?
questions.explanation:
Tab Settings on a profile control whether a tab is "Default On", "Default Off", or "Tab Hidden". Setting it to Tab Hidden removes the tab from the App Launcher and any default visible tabs, but doesn't strip the underlying object access — users can still reach the records via reports, related lists, list views, etc.

Object Permissions strip CRUD entirely (records become inaccessible). App Permissions and Org-Wide Defaults aren't tab-visibility levers. Tab Settings is the precise UI-only hide.

questions.text: The administrator for AW Computing is working with a user who is having trouble logging in to Salesforce. What should the administrator do to identify why the user is unable to log in?
questions.explanation:
The Login History (Setup > Login History) shows recent attempts including successful logins, failures, and the reason for failure (wrong password, IP not allowed, locked, etc.). It's the first investigative step when a user reports they can't log in.

Setup Audit Trail tracks setup changes. Password history is for policy enforcement. Resetting the security token may be a fix but isn't diagnostic. Login History is the targeted tool for "why can't this user log in?".

choices.label: A
choices.text: Review the login history for the user.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Check the attempted logins by running the setup audit trail.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Pull the password history to ensure the password policy was followed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reset the security token for the profile.

questions.text: A user at Northern Trail Outfitters is having trouble logging into Salesforce. The user's login history shows that this person has attempted to log in multiple times and has been locked out of the organization. Which two ways should the administrator help the user log into Salesforce? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two operations get a locked-out user back in. Resetting the password (which auto-unlocks too) gets them a temporary one. Clicking the Unlock button on their user record clears the lockout without changing their password. Either or both restores access.

Login-as-the-user doesn't reset/unlock. Password policy changes don't unlock individual users. Reset Password and Unlock are the two operative buttons on the user detail page.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Log in as the user to unlock the user and reset the password.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reset the password policies to allow the user to login.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Reset password on the user's record detail page.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the unlock button on the user's record detail page.

questions.text: A Sales user is trying to manage Campaign Members for an upcoming networking event. The user can view the Campaign, but cannot add new Campaign Members or update Member statuses. How can an administrator troubleshoot this problem?
questions.explanation:
The Marketing User feature license enables a user to manage Campaign Members, edit campaigns, configure advanced campaign setup, and import leads. The "Marketing User" checkbox on the user record record reflects whether they have this license. If unchecked, even Edit on Campaigns won't enable campaign-member management.

Permission set on Campaign Member, profile access to Leads/Contacts, and Data Loader workarounds don't substitute for the Marketing User license. Verifying the checkbox is checked is the first fix.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a permission set to allow the user to edit Campaign Members.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Provide the user access to both Leads and Contacts to edit all Members.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Make sure the Marketing User Checkbox is checked on the user record page.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run a Campaign report and update any Member information via Data Loader.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar provides a 1-year warranty on all of the panels it installs. Installation details, along with the warranty information, are captured on a custom object called Installation. The installation record is created by the installer from the mobile app. Customers can receive a longer warranty as a way of increasing customer satisfaction when an installation gets delayed or has issues. How should the administrator configure Salesforce to capture the expiration date of the warranty?
questions.explanation:
A formula as the default value of Warranty Expiration Date computes one year out from the install date at insert. Use DATE(YEAR(Installation_Date__c) + 1, MONTH(Installation_Date__c), DAY(Installation_Date__c)) (with sensible handling of Feb 29) as the default value formula. The field becomes editable, so customer service can override for extended warranties.

A standalone formula field can compute it on read but isn't editable for overrides. A validation rule doesn't populate. Surfacing on the mobile layout is the UX, not the population. Formula default value is the right combination of automatic + override-able.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use a formula as the default value of the warranty Expiration Date field.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a formula field to display 1 year from the warranty purchased.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add a validation rule to ensure the Expiration Date field is populated.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Include the warranty Expiration Date field on the mobile page layout.

questions.text: The IT manager at Universal Containers is doing an audit of the system's security. How should the administrator provide a summary of the org's security health?
questions.explanation:
Salesforce Health Check (Setup > Health Check) compares the org's security settings against a baseline (Salesforce-recommended or custom) and produces a score plus prioritized issues. It's the right artifact for "summary of org's security health".

OWDs hide records but don't summarize the security posture. Event Monitoring tracks user events. Login data is one input, not a summary. Health Check is the dedicated security-summary tool.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Change the Organization-Wide Default to private to restrict visibility.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Turn on Event Monitoring to track user events.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Download the last six months of user login data.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Run a Health Check to identify vulnerabilities.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks is introducing a new shoe model and wants to advertise on TV, radio, print, and social under the banner of a campaign called New Runners. In addition, total statistics for this marketing effort need to be aggregated and visible. Which feature should the administrator use to implement this functionality?
questions.explanation:
The Parent Campaign Field on Campaign creates a hierarchy. Make a parent campaign called "New Runners" and child campaigns for TV, radio, print, and social. Standard campaign-hierarchy roll-up fields (campaigns in hierarchy, total cost, won opps, etc.) aggregate across the children automatically.

Junction object is for many-to-many. Lookup or master-detail wouldn't roll up the campaign hierarchy fields built for this purpose. Parent Campaign Field is the right primitive.

questions.text: AW Computing has added a new custom text field called Market Segment on the Lead object. When a Lead is converted, the new field is not getting copied to the Account record. What should the administrator do to ensure the Market Segment field from a Lead is copied to the converted Account record routinely?
questions.explanation:
The fix is to add the Lead → Account mapping under Setup > Object Manager > Lead > Map Lead Fields. Until you explicitly map the new custom Lead.Market_Segment__c to a custom Account.Market_Segment__c, lead conversion won't carry the value. Sometimes you also need to ensure the Account field exists with a compatible type — but the operative step is the field mapping.

Same-name fields aren't auto-mapped. Validation rules and triggered flows can patch but the canonical solution is field mapping at conversion. Map the lead field is the answer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ensure the Market Segment field on the Lead is mapped to the right field on Account.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ensure Account has a field that has the exact same name as the new Lead field.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Write a Validation Rule to ensure the Account has a value in that field.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Write a record-triggered flow to copy the custom field from Lead to Account.

questions.text: Sales managers would like to know what could be implemented to surface important values based on the stage of the opportunity. Which tool should an administrator use to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Path's Key Fields panel surfaces stage-relevant fields directly inline. Reps see exactly the fields that matter for the current stage, with optional guidance text — no scrolling needed.

Opportunity processes (sales processes) define the stage list, not the surfaced fields. Dynamic Forms apply to record-page field placement broadly. Workflow Rules don't surface fields. Path Key Fields is the right tool.

questions.text: Support reps at Cloud Kicks (CK) are reporting that when they try to close a case, the Closed option in the Case Status picklist is missing. CK has asked the administrator to find a solution. Why are the support reps unable to see the Closed option in the specified picklist?
questions.explanation:
The Support Process bound to that record type controls which Case Status values are offered. If "Closed" is missing from the picklist, it's because the support process being used has not included Closed as one of the allowed status values for that record type.

The record type by itself doesn't define the status subset — its support process does. The Close Case page layout is a different layout used during the close action, not the cause. The "Show Closed Statuses" checkbox affects the Status combo on the Close Case page, not the Status picklist's available values. The support process is the operative subset definer.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Case record type is missing Closed as a picklist value.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Close Case page layout must be used to close a case.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Show Closed Statuses in Case Status Field checkbox is set to the default.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Support Process being used omits Closed as a status choice.

questions.text: A user has scheduled a Chatter post for 30 days from now and is then deactivated 10 days later. What will happen to the Chatter post in this situation?
questions.explanation:
A Chatter post scheduled for a future date is tied to the user's account. If the user is deactivated before the scheduled send time, the pending post is canceled and never delivered. Reactivating the user later doesn't re-queue it.

Sent on the 10th, paused, or sent in 30 days are all incorrect — deactivation cancels pending automation owned by the user. Cancellation is the documented behavior.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The pending Chatter post will be canceled.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The pending Chatter post will be sent on the 10th of the month

choices.label: C
choices.text: The pending Chatter post will be paused.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The pending Chatter post will be sent in 30 days.

questions.text: The administrator has created new users for ten new employees at Northern Trail Outfitters. Why are these users unable to access the account object in the Salesforce org?
questions.explanation:
Without object-level Read on Account, no other configuration matters. Profiles (or permission sets) must grant Account permission first. Sharing rules, hierarchies, and OWDs only apply once profile-level access is granted.

Sharing rules, role hierarchy, and OWDs are about which records the user sees among those their profile permits — they can't elevate above object-level grants. Profile permission to the object is the prerequisite.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Users' profile requires a sharing rule for Accounts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Users' profile requires permission to the Account object.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Users' roles are low on the role hierarchy.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Organization-wide defaults are set to private.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks (CK) stores information about specific customers in Contacts and information about shoes and accessories in a custom Merchandise object. What should the CK administrator use to represent that a Contact can be interested in multiple pieces of Merchandise?
questions.explanation:
A Junction Object — a custom object with master-detail relationships to both Contact and Merchandise — models the many-to-many. Each junction record represents one "this contact is interested in this merchandise" pairing. Reports and related lists work cleanly off the junction.

Hierarchy column is for self-relationships. Lookup filter constrains pickers, not modeling. Formula fields don't link records. Junction object is the canonical many-to-many shape.

questions.text: The administrator at Universal Containers has created two objects: Containers and Purchase. Management has requested that all container records display on purchase records in Salesforce. Which type of relationship between Containers and Purchase should satisfy the requirement?
questions.explanation:
A Lookup field on the Purchase object pointing to Container creates the relationship. With the lookup in place, a Containers related list appears on the Purchase record (or you can add one explicitly), letting you see the related containers from the purchase page.

Roll-Up Summary requires master-detail and aggregates, not lists. Formula fields don't link records. Master-detail couples the records too tightly for "many independent purchases referencing containers". Lookup is the right relationship type.

questions.text: The Marketing team at Cloud Kicks uses campaigns to generate product interest. They want custom picklist values for the Campaign Member Status field for each campaign they run. Currently, they ask the administrator to add or delete values, but this is very time consuming. Which two user permissions should allow the Marketing team to customize the Campaign Member Status picklist values themselves? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two specific privileges let marketers manage campaign-member statuses themselves. The Marketing User feature license (the "Marketing User" checkbox on the user record) plus Edit permission on the Campaign object give them everything needed to add/edit campaign-member statuses for each campaign they run.

Create/Edit on Campaign Member alone is insufficient. Customize Application is too broad. Marketing User license + Edit on Campaign is the right pair.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create and Edit for Campaign Member

questions.text: Universal Containers wants to provide reseller partners with discounted prices on the products they purchase. How should an administrator configure this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A separate Price Book for reseller partners holds the discounted prices. Add the partner Price Book Entries (one per product) at the discounted Price; reps quoting reseller deals choose the partner price book and the discounted prices apply automatically.

A Partner_Discount__c field requires hand-calculations. Separate products multiply maintenance. Different record types organize but don't price. Separate Price Book is the canonical pricing-tier solution.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add a Partner_Discount__c field to the Opportunity

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use a different Opportunity record type.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a separate PriceBook for reseller partners.

questions.text: Ursa Major classifies its accounts as Silver, Gold, or Platinum Level. When a new case is created for a Silver or Gold partner, it should go to the Regular Support Queue. When an account is Platinum Level, it should automatically go to the Priority Support Queue. What should the administrator use to achieve this?
questions.explanation:
Case Assignment Rules can route based on field criteria. Rules with conditions on Account.Type (or a related Account-tier field) push Silver/Gold cases to the Regular Support Queue and Platinum cases to the Priority Support Queue automatically on case create.

"Case Rules" isn't a feature. Workflow Rules can't change owner during case create as cleanly. Escalation Rules act after age. Assignment Rules are the right routing primitive.

questions.text: The standard Lead Rating field has picklist values of Hot, Warm, and Cold. A list of new leads was imported without errors even though several records had the value of Unrated in the Rating field. How were these records added without error?
questions.explanation:
A picklist with the Restricted setting blocks any value outside the defined picklist values from being saved — at the API or UI level. With Restricted unchecked, imports and integrations can write arbitrary values into the picklist field, including unlisted ones like "Unrated".

Field-Level Security controls visibility, not write validation. Global picklist value sets enforce values across fields when restricted. Add to All Record Types extends, not validates. Restricted picklist toggle is the operative valid-value control.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Restricted picklist checkbox was unchecked.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Field-level security was set to Visible for all profiles.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A global picklist value set was used to populate the picklist.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Add to All Record Types checkbox was selected.

questions.text: The administrator at AW Consulting has created a custom picklist field. Business users have requested that it be a text field. The administrator attempts to change the field type but is unable to because it is referenced by other functionalities. Which functionality is preventing the field type from being changed?
questions.explanation:
Formula fields reference other fields, including the field type they evaluate. If a formula somewhere references a custom picklist field with a function specific to picklists (TEXT(picklist), ISPICKVAL(...) etc.), changing the type to text breaks the formula. Salesforce blocks the type change to protect those references.

Record types reference picklist values, not field type. Visualforce and JavaScript references are typically warned about but don't block the type change as universally. A formula reference is the most common blocker.

questions.text: What data loss considerations should an administrator keep in mind when changing a custom field type from Text to Picklist? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two real considerations when changing Text → Picklist. Assignment and escalation rules with criteria based on the field may behave differently because the type's compare semantics change (text matching vs picklist value matching). Any list view filtered on the old text field with values not in the new picklist gets deleted because those filter values are no longer valid.

Global value sets are unrelated. Visualforce auto-updates aren't a thing. Assignment/escalation impact + list view deletion are the real consequences.

choices.label: A
choices.text: There will be no data loss with use of a global value set.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assignment and escalation rules may be affected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Auto updates will be made to Visualforce references to prevent data loss.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Any list view based on the custom field is deleted.

questions.text: Marketing users at Cloud Kicks should be able to view and edit converted leads. The administrator has assigned them a permission set with the View and Edit Converted Leads permission. Which two ways can the marketing users now access converted leads for editing? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two paths to the converted leads with the View and Edit Converted Leads permission set. They show up in Global Search results (the search index returns them; the perm allows opening them). They also appear in any List View whose criteria include them — e.g. one filtered to Lead Status = Qualified shows the qualified-and-converted records.

Recent Records and Data Import Wizard aren't search/access methods. Global Search + Lead Status list view are the practical access paths.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Find them in the global search result.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Search the Recent Records component on the homepage.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Utilize a list view where lead status equals Qualified.

questions.text: Universal Containers has a private sharing model for Opportunities and uses Opportunity teams. Criteria-based sharing rules. A sales rep at Universal Containers leaves the company and their user record is deactivated. The rep is later rehired. The administrator activates the old user record. The user is added to the same default Opportunity teams but is no longer able to view records the user worked on before leaving the company. What is the likely cause?
questions.explanation:
Manual sharing is removed when the original owner changes (e.g., on user deactivation). When the user is later reactivated and re-added to default Opportunity teams, those team-based shares come back, but the manual shares (one-off "share this record with this user" entries) do not — they were silently removed during deactivation.

Stage changes, permission set removals, or record-type changes don't explain the team-restored-but-records-missing pattern. Manual sharing being removed is the typical cause.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The stage of the Opportunity records was changed to closed lost.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Permission sets were removed when the user was deactivated.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The record type of the Opportunity records was changed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The records were manually shared with the user.

questions.text: Ursa Major Solar wants its sales reps to be aware when they are speaking with high-profile customers. Which two options should be added to the Lightning record pages to achieve this? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two Lightning App Builder building blocks deliver the "VIP awareness" UX. A Custom Component (an LWC or Aura built for this) renders a banner or visual cue based on the contact's profile (e.g. account type or VIP flag). Component Visibility Filters then ensure the component appears only when the relevant fields indicate VIP — sales reps see a clear cue precisely when they should.

Highlight Panel and Action and Recommendations show standard items. Rich Text Area is static. Custom Component + Component Visibility Filter is the right combination for "show this only when X".

questions.text: What should an administrator use as an identifier when importing and updating records from a separate system?
questions.explanation:
An External ID field stores a unique identifier from a foreign system. With an External ID column, upsert operations match incoming rows against existing records by external ID, so you don't need Salesforce IDs in your import file.

Rich text, record ID, and auto-number aren't external-system match keys. External ID is the standard mechanism for cross-system imports.

questions.text: The CTO of AW Computing has defined a new policy for cases to improve customer satisfaction. All cases submitted with a Case Reason of Installation must be acknowledged immediately via email and assigned to the appropriate agents. Any cases that are still in the New status after 4 hours must be escalated to support management. What case management tools need to be utilized for this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Three case management primitives line up with the requirement. Auto-Response Rules send the immediate acknowledgment email when a Case Reason = 'Installation' case is created. Queues group those installation cases for the right team. Case Escalation Rules then escalate any case that's still New after 4 hours to support management.

Macros are agent-side shortcuts, not auto-acknowledgment. Entitlements drive SLA timing but aren't the response/escalation mechanisms here. Auto-Response + Queue + Escalation Rule is the right trio.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks generates leads for its different product categories (shoes, apparel, and accessories) through many different sources. While some lead sources are used for all three categories, other lead sources are specific to a single category. The VP of marketing requests that only the proper lead sources be displayed based on the product category chosen. How should the administrator configure Salesforce to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
A Field Dependency between Product Category (controlling) and Lead Source (dependent) restricts which Lead Source values are visible per category. The picklist UI automatically filters the available Lead Sources based on the selected category — no record types, no flow.

Page layouts don't filter picklist values. Business processes/record types are heavier. Field dependency is the precise feature for "show only relevant picklist values based on another field".

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a page layout for each category and filter the Lead Source field based on category.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a dependency between the Product Category field and Lead Source field.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create business processes and record types for each of the three product categories.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a single business process, then create record types for each product category.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks (CK) needs a new sales application. The administrator finds an application package on the AppExchange and wants to begin testing it in a sandbox to see if it addresses CK's needs. What are two considerations when installing a managed package in a sandbox? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two specifics for installing managed packages in a sandbox. The installation URL must be pointed at test.salesforce.com (instead of login.salesforce.com) — packages know the difference. And the package will be removed if the sandbox is later refreshed from production (since the refresh wipes everything that's not in production).

Metadata-changes-recreated isn't true (changes flow with the package). Install for Admins Only isn't the only option. URL-must-be-test + sandbox-refresh-clears-package are the right two considerations.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Any metadata changes to the package have to be recreated in production.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The installation link has to be modified to test.salesforce.com.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Install for Admins Only will be the only Install option available.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The package will be removed any time the sandbox is refreshed.

questions.text: The administrator at Northern Trail Outfitters has been using a spreadsheet to track assigned licenses and permission sets. What feature can be used to track this in Salesforce?
questions.explanation:
A Standard User Report shows users by license type, profile, role, status, and other administrative fields. Combined with permission set assignment fields/lists, you get a single source of truth for who has what license — replacing the spreadsheet with a saved report.

Login History tracks logins, not licenses. Lightning Usage App tracks adoption metrics. Permission Set Groups bundle access; they don't report. User Report is the targeted feature.

questions.text: Customer service accesses articles with the Knowledge Lightning component on the Service Cloud Console. Billing department users would like similar functionality on the case record without using the console. How should the administrator configure this request?
questions.explanation:
Adding the Knowledge Related List to the Case page layout surfaces relevant articles right on the page, regardless of console mode. Without console-only components, the related list is a perfectly good way to expose Knowledge content on a record page used outside the console.

Adding a "Knowledge component" or "Knowledge component list" outside the console isn't the right delivery. The Knowledge Related List on the page layout is the canonical way for non-console access.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Add the Knowledge component to the page layout.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Add the Knowledge component list to the page layout.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add the Knowledge related list to the page layout.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add the Knowledge related list to the record page

questions.text: Brokers at DreamHouse Realty need to see certain information about one or more cases when referencing the contact record. This includes Case Name, Case ID, Customer Name, Case Reason, Case Status, and Case Creation Date. Which two changes in Setup should the administrator make? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two adjustments deliver the customized cases related list on the Contact record page. In the Lightning App Builder, edit the Related List component and set its type to Related List (the rich, page-layout-driven version). Then in the Page Layout Editor, configure the Cases related list's columns to include Case Name, Case ID, Customer Name, Reason, Status, and Created Date.

Enhanced List type is more compact and limits column-set richness. Page-layout-Enhanced List is a different combo. Related List type + page layout column config is the right pair.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Use the page layout editor to change the related list type to Enhanced List.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Edit the Related List component in the Lightning App Builder and choose Related List as the related list type.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Edit the Related List component in the Lightning App Builder and choose Enhanced List as the related list type.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the page layout editor to include the appropriate column in the Cases related list.

questions.text: DreamHouse Realty requires that house showings be scheduled within the current year to prevent too many future showings from stacking up. How can they make sure Showing Date is only populated with a date this year?
questions.explanation:
A Validation Rule with formula YEAR(Showing_Date__c) <> YEAR(TODAY()) blocks any save where the date isn't in the current year. Users see the error immediately on save attempts.

Calendar sync, post-hoc reports, and help text don't prevent the bad save. Validation Rule is the targeted enforcement mechanism.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sync the users' Showing Calendar to Salesforce and filter it to only look at this year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create a report that shows any Showing Dates not scheduled in the current year to be updated.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add Help Text so the user knows to only add a Showing Date within the current year.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create a validation rule that ensures Showing Date contains a date within the current year.

questions.text: The administrator at Cloud Kicks writes an assignment rule to send all cases created via email or the web to the Automated Cases Queue. Any manually created cases should be owned by the agent creating them. However, the manually created cases now show the administrator as the owner. What will the administrator find when troubleshooting this issue?
questions.explanation:
The "Default to Active Assignment Rule" checkbox on the Case page layout (or the Use Default Assignment Rule toggle) controls whether new manual cases run through assignment rules. If it's selected by default, even manually created cases get reassigned by the rule, leaving the admin as the inadvertent owner instead of the agent.

Escalation rules don't act on case create. Other assignment rules and missing form fields aren't the cause. The default-active checkbox is the operative cause to investigate.

choices.label: A
choices.text: An escalation rule is changing the case owner on case creation

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Assignment Rule checkbox is selected by default.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Another assignment rule is giving ownership to the administrator

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Owner field is missing on the webform and email template.

questions.text: Cloud Kicks (CK) captures whether an opportunity should be reviewed by someone in product engineering with a checkbox field called Needs Review. CK also has a picklist field on the opportunity for Product Type. When a sales rep saves an opportunity, they need to select the Product Type or check the Needs Review box. What should an administrator use to accomplish this?
questions.explanation:
A Validation Rule with formula AND(ISBLANK(TEXT(Product_Type__c)), Needs_Review__c = FALSE) blocks the save unless one of those is set. Single rule, OR-style logic via the AND/ISBLANK pattern.

Before-save flow can do it but a validation rule is the precise data-quality primitive. Workflow Rule can't block save. Required-fields applies to both unconditionally. Validation Rule is the targeted answer.

questions.text: The Support team at Ursa Major Solar prefers using split list views on the case homepage. Occasionally, the team views shipments from another support application. What should the administrator configure to allow the team to use the split list view?
questions.explanation:
Split List Views are supported on standard objects only. The case homepage allows split view because Case is standard. The custom Shipments object (or shipment custom objects) doesn't support split view, so an admin can't enable it for that view — the team's only options for shipments are standard or Kanban list views.

Filtering and tab placement don't enable split view on custom objects. Manage List Views is unrelated. Split-views-only-on-standard-objects is the operative platform constraint.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Filter by a single shipment record type in the list view.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Include the Shipments tab on the app's navigation bar.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Split views are only available on standard objects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Add the Manage List Views permission for support users.

questions.text: DreamHouse Realty regularly holds open houses for the selling of both houses and condominiums. For condominium open houses, there are a few extra steps that need to be taken. Agents need to be able to submit requests and receive approvals from the homeowners' association. How can the administrator ensure these extra steps only appear when creating open house records for condominiums?
questions.explanation:
Two Page Layouts — one for House open houses, one for Condominium open houses — paired with a Business Process per record type that exposes the right Status values means each kind of open house guides agents through its specific approval steps. Record types tie the right page layout and business process to each.

Single-page-layout approaches don't separate the workflows. Two layouts + record types + business processes is the right shape.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create one page layout. Use record types to ensure the proper status picklist values display.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Create two page layouts. Use business processes and record types to display the appropriate picklist values.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Create one page layout. Use business processes to ensure the proper status picklist values display.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create two page layouts, one with a House Status field and the other with a Condominium Status field.

questions.text: An administrator at Ursa Major Solar just learned about the AppExchange and how helpful it can be to the company's business. Which two actions can be accomplished via the AppExchange? (Choose 2)
questions.explanation:
Two valid AppExchange use cases. Find certified Consultants in the consulting directory — vetted partners for project work. Install industry-specific Solution Templates (managed packages) that pre-build dashboards, objects, and flows for verticals like manufacturing or healthcare.

Data Loader is downloaded from Setup, not AppExchange. Standard Lightning components ship with the platform, not via AppExchange. Consultants + industry solution templates are the right two outcomes.

questions.text: An administrator is building a Lightning app and sees a message that My Domain must be set up first. What should the administrator take into consideration when enabling My Domain?
questions.explanation:
Enabling My Domain changes the login URL for everyone — internal and external — to the My Domain URL. Internal users get redirected; external (community/Experience Cloud) users authenticate via the My Domain too. That's the most important behavioral change to plan for.

SSO can coexist with My Domain. My Domain is changeable later (renamable). The URL changes per release in some cases. The big consideration is the universal login URL change.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Single sign-on must be disabled prior to implementing My Domain.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The login for all internal and external users changes to the My Domain login

choices.label: C
choices.text: A deployed My Domain is irreversible and renaming is unavailable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The URL instance for a My Domain stays the same for every release

questions.text: Which page layouts will have the Individual field available for tracking data privacy information when Data Protection and Privacy is enabled?
questions.explanation:
When Data Protection and Privacy is enabled, the Individual object exists to hold privacy preferences (consent, opt-out flags, etc.). The Individual lookup field becomes available on the three "person" objects: Contact, Lead, and Person Account. That trio is where you can attach an Individual and govern privacy.

Case, Opportunity, Account (business), User, and Individual itself don't get the lookup. Contact + Lead + Person Account is the canonical set.
